1→# CLAUDE.md
     2→
     3→This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
     4→
     5→## Project Overview
     6→
     7→Synapse v5.3.0 is an AI-Houdini Bridge — a standalone Python package (zero required dependencies) that lets AI assistants control SideFX Houdini via WebSocket. It exposes 43 MCP tools to Claude Desktop/Code for real-time scene manipulation, persistent project memory, adaptive tiered LLM routing, and viewport/render capture.
     8→
     9→Two repos make up the full system:
    10→- **`C:\Users\User\Synapse\`** — Core server, protocol, handlers, memory, routing, MCP bridge
    11→- **`C:\Users\User\.synapse\`** — Agent SDK (autonomous co-pilot), design system (tokens/icons/styles), Houdini shelf/panel integration, installer
    12→
    13→---
    14→
    15→## Sprint Orchestrator — Auto-Detecting
    16→
    17→> **How this works:** On every session start, check the filesystem gates below to determine
    18→> which sprint is active. No manual status flipping required — the codebase IS the state.
    19→
    20→### Step 1: Check MCP Sprint Gates
    21→
    22→Verify ALL of the following files exist in the repo:
    23→
    24→```
    25→python/synapse/mcp/server.py   — MCP endpoint handler with /mcp route
    26→python/synapse/mcp/tools.py    — Tool registry mapping to existing handlers
    27→python/synapse/mcp/session.py  — Session manager
    28→python/synapse/mcp/protocol.py — JSON-RPC utilities
    29→docs/mcp/SETUP.md              — User-facing connection instructions
    30→tests/test_mcp_protocol.py     — MCP protocol tests (must exist AND pass)
    31→```
    32→
    33→**Run this check:**
    34→```bash
    35→# All 6 must exist. If ANY is missing, MCP Sprint is active.
    36→ls python/synapse/mcp/server.py python/synapse/mcp/tools.py python/synapse/mcp/session.py \
    37→   python/synapse/mcp/protocol.py docs/mcp/SETUP.md tests/test_mcp_protocol.py
    38→```
    39→
    40→### Step 2: Route to Active Sprint
    41→
    42→```
    43→IF any MCP gate file is missing:
    44→    → ACTIVE SPRINT: MCP Protocol Conformance
    45→    → Read: docs/mcp/SYNAPSE_MCP_SPRINT.md
    46→    → TOPS status: PARKED (do NOT touch TOPS/PDG files)
    47→
    48→ELSE IF MCP gates pass BUT tops tools not registered:
    49→    (Check: grep -l "tops_cook_node\|tops_get_work_items" python/synapse/mcp/tools.py → no match)
    50→    → ACTIVE SPRINT: TOPS/PDG Integration
    51→    → Read: docs/tops/TOPS_SPRINT.md
    52→    → Read: docs/tops/PARKING_SNAPSHOT.md (resume context)
    53→    → Agent orchestration: ~/.claude/agent.md
    54→
    55→ELSE (both MCP and TOPS gates pass):
    56→    → NO ACTIVE SPRINT — normal development mode
    57→    → All new functionality follows "Adding New Functionality" below
    58→```
    59→
    60→---
    61→
    62→### Sprint A: MCP Protocol Conformance
    63→
    64→**Activates when:** Any MCP gate file is missing.
    65→
    66→> **Goal:** Add MCP Streamable HTTP transport to SYNAPSE, making it a universal MCP server
    67→> that any compliant client (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, etc.) can connect to
    68→> via `claude mcp add --transport http synapse http://localhost:PORT/mcp`.
    69→>
    70→> **Why now:** MCP is a force-multiplier. Every tool, resource, and feature SYNAPSE exposes
    71→> becomes available to the entire AI tooling ecosystem — not just our WebSocket clients.
    72→> Every subsequent feature (including TOPS) benefits immediately.
    73→>
    74→> **Protocol Target:** MCP 2025-06-18 (Streamable HTTP, JSON-RPC 2.0)
    75→
    76→#### MCP Sprint Phases
    77→
    78→| Phase | Scope | Gate Files |
    79→|-------|-------|------------|
    80→| **Phase 1 — MVP** | `/mcp` endpoint, JSON-RPC router, `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, session management | `server.py`, `tools.py`, `session.py`, `protocol.py` |
    81→| **Phase 2 — Resources & Prompts** | `resources/list`, `resources/read`, scene state exposure, prompt templates | `SETUP.md`, `test_mcp_protocol.py` |
    82→| **Phase 3 — Polish** | `list_changed` notifications, SSE stream, `resources/subscribe`, auth, rate limiting | (no new gate files — completes MCP sprint) |
    83→
    84→**Before starting any phase, read `docs/mcp/SYNAPSE_MCP_SPRINT.md`** for full implementation
    85→reference including code examples, the complete JSON-RPC router, tool registry pattern,
    86→FastMCP SDK integration options, and protocol details.
    87→
    88→#### MCP Sprint Rules
    89→
    90→1. **The MCP layer is a protocol adapter** — it sits on top of existing handlers and safety middleware. It does NOT replace them.
    91→2. **Existing endpoints are untouched** — WebSocket transport, REST adapter, and all current functionality continue to work.
    92→3. **New files go in `synapse/mcp/`** — see File Organization below. Do not scatter MCP protocol code across existing modules.
    93→4. **All tool calls route through existing `handlers.py`** — the MCP dispatch layer translates JSON-RPC into existing SYNAPSE commands. Safety middleware (atomic scripts, idempotent guards, undo-groups) is enforced by the handlers, never bypassed.
    94→5. **Test without Houdini** — MCP protocol tests follow the same `hou` stub pattern as existing tests.
    95→
    96→#### TOPS — PARKED During MCP Sprint
    97→
    98→**While MCP sprint is active, TOPS is frozen:**
    99→
   100→- Do NOT modify any TOPS/PDG files as part of MCP work
   101→- Do NOT refactor TOPS-related code during this sprint
   102→- If MCP implementation reveals a natural interface point for TOPS, document it in `docs/mcp/TOPS_INTEGRATION_POINTS.md` but do not implement
   103→- All TOPS-related branches remain as-is — no rebasing, no merging
   104→
   105→**On first run of MCP sprint:** Scan the codebase for any TOPS/PDG work-in-progress. Write a parking snapshot to `docs/tops/PARKING_SNAPSHOT.md` capturing: where it was, what was being worked on, immediate next action, and blockers. This snapshot is consumed at TOPS sprint resumption.
   106→
   107→---
   108→
   109→### Sprint B: TOPS/PDG Integration
   110→
   111→**Activates when:** All MCP gate files exist AND TOPS tools are not yet registered in `mcp/tools.py`.
   112→
   113→> **Goal:** Add PDG/TOPs integration to SYNAPSE, exposing distributed cooking, wedging,
   114→> dependency management, and scheduler control as MCP tools. Every TOPS capability is
   115→> registered in the MCP tool registry from day one — no separate API, no retrofit.
   116→>
   117→> **Prerequisite:** MCP Protocol Sprint must be complete (verified by filesystem gates above).
   118→
   119→#### On TOPS Sprint Activation
   120→
   121→1. **Read `docs/tops/TOPS_SPRINT.md`** — full implementation reference with tool schemas, handler patterns, PDG API surface, and phased plan
   122→2. **Read `docs/tops/PARKING_SNAPSHOT.md`** — resume context from when TOPS was parked
   123→3. **Read `docs/mcp/TOPS_INTEGRATION_POINTS.md`** (if it exists) — integration hints noted during MCP sprint
   124→4. **Load `~/.claude/agent.md`** — agent orchestration directives for TOPS sub-tasks (`C:\Users\User\.claude\agent.md`)
   125→
   126→#### TOPS Sprint Phases
   127→
   128→| Phase | Scope | Verification |
   129→|-------|-------|-------------|
   130→| **Phase 1 — Core Tools** | `tops_get_work_items`, `tops_get_dependency_graph`, `tops_get_cook_stats`, `tops_cook_node`, `tops_generate_items` | Tools appear in `tools/list` from MCP client |
   131→| **Phase 2 — Scheduler & Control** | `tops_configure_scheduler`, `tops_cancel_cook`, `tops_dirty_node`, TOPS resources | Scheduler configurable via MCP, cook cancellable |
   132→| **Phase 3 — Advanced** | Wedge setup, batch cook, work item queries, cook progress notifications | End-to-end PDG workflow from MCP client |
   133→
   134→#### TOPS Sprint Rules
   135→
   136→1. **All TOPS tools register as MCP tools from the start** — use the `mcp/tools.py` registry pattern. No separate API.
   137→2. **Handlers go in `handlers.py`** alongside existing handlers — follow the exact same pattern.
   138→3. **Safety middleware applies automatically** — TOPS handlers inherit atomic scripts, idempotent guards, undo-groups.
   139→4. **Stub `pdg` module in tests** — same pattern as `hou` stubs. `import pdg` only works inside Houdini.
   140→5. **Both MCP registries stay in sync** — `mcp_server.py` (stdio) and `mcp/tools.py` (Streamable HTTP).
   141→
   142→#### TOPS Sprint Completion Gate
   143→
   144→Sprint B is complete when `grep -c "tops_" synapse/mcp/tools.py` returns 5+ (core tools registered)
   145→AND `python -m pytest tests/test_tops.py -v` passes.
   146→
   147→#### Agent Orchestration
   148→
   149→TOPS work can be decomposed into agent sub-tasks. See `.claude/agent.md` for directives
   150→on how to structure TOPS implementation as agent work items. See `~/.claude/agent.md`
   151→(`C:\Users\User\.claude\agent.md`).
   152→
   153→---
   154→
   155→### Sprint Queue (Future)
   156→
   157→When both Sprint A and Sprint B are complete, the orchestrator enters normal development mode.
   158→Potential future sprints can be added here with their own filesystem gates:
   159→
   160→```
   161→Sprint C: Agent SDK v2 (autonomous VFX co-pilot improvements)
   162→Sprint D: Studio deployment (multi-user auth, remote access, RBAC)
   163→Sprint E: Real-time monitoring (live scene metrics dashboard)
   164→```
   165→
   166→To add a new sprint: define filesystem gates, write a sprint doc in `docs/`, add a gate
   167→check block above, and the orchestrator picks it up automatically.
   168→
   169→---
   170→
   171→## Source vs. Deployed Files
   172→
   173→**Always edit the repo source — never the deployed copies.** The installer (`~/.synapse/install.py`) copies from source to Houdini prefs. Editing deployed files directly causes drift that gets overwritten on next install.
   174→
   175→| What | Source (edit here) | Deployed (never edit) |
   176→|------|-------------------|----------------------|
   177→| Core server | `SYNAPSE/python/synapse/` | `site-packages/synapse/` |
   178→| Shelf/panel | `~/.synapse/houdini/` | `~/houdini21.0/` |
   179→| Design system | `~/.synapse/design/` | (not deployed) |

   230→## Architecture
   231→
   232→### Data Flow (MCP to Houdini)
   233→
   234→```
   235→ANY MCP Client (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, custom agents)
   236→    |  Streamable HTTP: POST/GET http://localhost:PORT/mcp
   237→    |  JSON-RPC 2.0 + Mcp-Session-Id headers
   238→    |
   239→MCP Protocol Layer  (synapse/mcp/ — NEW)
   240→    |  Session mgmt, tool/resource/prompt dispatch
   241→    |  Translates JSON-RPC ↔ SYNAPSE commands
   242→    |
   243→    ├─── tools/call ──────┐
   244→    ├─── resources/read ──┤
   245→    └─── prompts/get ─────┤
   246→                          |
   247→Claude Desktop/Code       |  (existing stdio path preserved)
   248→    |  stdio / JSON-RPC   |
   249→mcp_server.py  (43 tools) |
   250→    |                     |
   251→    ├─────────────────────┘
   252→    |  WebSocket: ws://localhost:9999/synapse
   253→SynapseServer  (daemon thread inside Houdini)
   254→    |  CommandHandlerRegistry (handlers.py)
   255→hou.* Python API
   256→    |
   257→Houdini USD Stage / Solaris / Karma
   258→```
   259→
   260→Both MCP Streamable HTTP and the existing WebSocket/stdio paths converge at the same handler layer. The MCP protocol layer adds no new safety logic — it delegates entirely to existing handlers which enforce atomic scripts, idempotent guards, and undo-group transactions.
   261→
   262→### Core Package Layout (`python/synapse/`)
   263→
   264→| Layer | Directory | Responsibility |
   265→|-------|-----------|---------------|
   266→| Foundation | `core/` | Wire protocol (`protocol.py`), parameter aliases (`aliases.py`), determinism (`determinism.py`), audit chain (`audit.py`), human gates (`gates.py`), encryption (`crypto.py`), command queue (`queue.py`) |

   268→| Routing | `routing/` | Tiered LLM dispatch (`router.py`), regex parser (`parser.py`), RAG knowledge (`knowledge.py`), recipes (`recipes.py`), deterministic cache (`cache.py`), workflow planner (`planner.py`), epoch-based tier adaptation (`adaptation.py`) |
   269→| Agent | `agent/` | prepare/propose/execute/learn lifecycle (`executor.py`), task/plan/step protocol (`protocol.py`), outcome tracking (`learning.py`) |
   270→| **MCP** | **`mcp/`** | **MCP Streamable HTTP protocol layer (NEW). `server.py` (endpoint handler, JSON-RPC router), `session.py` (session manager), `tools.py` (tool registry mapping to existing handlers), `resources.py` (scene state resources), `prompts.py` (reusable workflow prompts), `protocol.py` (JSON-RPC utilities, error codes), `types.py` (type definitions, schemas)** |

   274→
   275→### Routing Cascade (cheapest-first)
   276→
   277→```
   278→Cache(O(1)) -> Recipe(O(1)) -> Planner(O(1)) -> Tier0/regex(O(n)) -> Tier1/RAG(O(log n)) -> Tier2/Haiku(~5s) -> Tier3/Agent(~15s)
   279→```
   280→
   281→- **Tier pinning** (He2025 consistency): Same input+context maps to same tier on subsequent calls. LRU cache, max 1,000 pins, stale pins fall through.
   282→- **Speculative T0+T1 parallelism**: Module-level `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2)` runs Tier 0 regex and Tier 1 knowledge lookup concurrently.
   283→- **Tier 1 result threading**: `route()` runs `knowledge.lookup()` once, threads the result to all higher tiers to avoid redundant lookups.
   284→
   285→### Transport Backends
   286→
   287→| Backend | Module | Transport | Latency | Use Case |
   288→|---------|--------|-----------|---------|----------|
   289→| `websockets` | `server/websocket.py` | WebSocket | ~0.2ms warm ping | Primary — reads, pings, everything |
   290→| `hwebserver` | `server/hwebserver_adapter.py` | HTTP (Houdini native) | ~2s floor (main event loop) | Optional — only for hou.* mutations |
   291→| **`mcp`** | **`mcp/server.py`** | **Streamable HTTP (MCP)** | **TBD** | **Universal MCP client access (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, etc.)** |
   292→
   293→WebSocket remains the primary internal transport. The MCP Streamable HTTP endpoint is additive — it provides a standardized protocol interface that any MCP-compliant client can use. Both share the same handler layer.
   294→
   295→### Authentication (`server/auth.py`)
   296→
   297→Optional API key authentication for both transports. Key sources (checked in order):
   298→1. `SYNAPSE_API_KEY` environment variable
   299→2. `~/.synapse/auth.key` file (first non-empty, non-comment line)
   300→3. No key configured -> auth disabled (backward compat)
   301→
   302→When enabled, first WebSocket message must be an `authenticate` command with `{"payload": {"key": "..."}}`. Uses `hmac.compare_digest` for constant-time comparison. Auth handshake integrated into both `websocket.py` and `hwebserver_adapter.py`.
   303→
   304→**MCP auth (Phase 3):** Bearer token authentication via `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header on the `/mcp` endpoint. Opt-in for remote/studio deployments. Not required for localhost connections. Implemented as a `TokenVerifier` that delegates to the existing `auth.py` key validation.
   305→
   306→### MCP Server — Existing stdio Bridge (`mcp_server.py`)
   307→
   308→38 tools. Key operational details:
   309→- **Concurrent dispatch**: `_pending` dict + `_recv_loop` coroutine — no blocking lock, true parallel tool calls
   310→- **Timeouts**: Default 10s. Overrides: execute_python/execute_vex/capture_viewport/inspect_* at 30s, render/wedge at 120s, batch at 60s
   311→- **JSON**: Uses `orjson` (fast, sort_keys via `OPT_SORT_KEYS`) when available, falls back to stdlib `json`
   312→- **Warmup**: Pre-connect in `main()` reduces first-call latency
   313→- **Retry**: `MAX_RETRIES=2`, `RETRY_DELAY=0.3`, auto-retry on connection drop
   314→- **Connection**: `open_timeout=3.0`, `ping_interval=None`, `compression=None` (localhost optimization)
   315→
   316→This existing stdio MCP bridge (`mcp_server.py`) is preserved as-is. The new MCP Streamable HTTP layer (`synapse/mcp/`) is a separate, additive transport — not a replacement.
   317→
   318→### MCP Protocol Layer — Streamable HTTP (NEW)
   319→
   320→This is the active sprint work. The MCP protocol layer lives in `synapse/mcp/` and provides a JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoint at `/mcp` on the hwebserver.
   321→
   322→#### Endpoint Behavior
   323→
   324→```
   325→POST /mcp   →  Client sends JSON-RPC request or notification
   326→               Response: application/json (single result) or text/event-stream (streaming)
   327→GET  /mcp   →  Opens optional SSE stream for server→client messages (Phase 3)
   328→```
   329→
   330→#### Session Lifecycle
   331→
   332→1. Client POSTs `initialize` with `clientInfo` and `protocolVersion`
   333→2. Server responds with capabilities, serverInfo, and `Mcp-Session-Id` header
   334→3. Client sends `notifications/initialized` (server returns 202 Accepted)
   335→4. Session is live — client can call `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `resources/read`, etc.
   336→5. Session ends when client disconnects or sends `notifications/cancelled`
   337→
   338→#### Initialize Response
   339→
   340→```python
   341→{
   342→    "protocolVersion": "2025-06-18",
   343→    "capabilities": {
   344→        "tools": {"listChanged": True},
   345→        "resources": {"subscribe": False, "listChanged": False},
   346→    },
   347→    "serverInfo": {
   348→        "name": "synapse",
   349→        "version": "5.3.0"
   350→    },
   351→    "instructions": (
   352→        "SYNAPSE is a bridge between AI agents and SideFX Houdini. "
   353→        "All mutations go through safety middleware enforcing atomic scripts, "
   354→        "idempotent guards, and undo-group transactions. "
   355→        "Tools marked destructiveHint=True modify the Houdini scene."
   356→    )
   357→}
   358→```
   359→
   360→#### Tool Registry — Mapping Existing Handlers
   361→
   362→Every existing SYNAPSE command handler maps 1:1 to an MCP tool. The `synapse/mcp/tools.py` module builds `tools/list` output from handler introspection and dispatches `tools/call` to the handler registry.
   363→
   364→Tool definitions include JSON Schema `inputSchema` and MCP `annotations`:
   365→
   366→```python
   367→{
   368→    "name": "execute_vex",
   369→    "description": "Execute VEX code on a wrangle node through SYNAPSE safety middleware.",
   370→    "inputSchema": {
   371→        "type": "object",
   372→        "properties": {
   373→            "code": {"type": "string", "description": "VEX source code"},
   374→            "node_path": {"type": "string", "description": "Full path to wrangle node"},
   375→            "run_over": {
   376→                "type": "string",
   377→                "enum": ["Points", "Vertices", "Primitives", "Detail"],
   378→                "default": "Points"
   379→            }
   380→        },
   381→        "required": ["code", "node_path"]
   382→    },
   383→    "annotations": {
   384→        "title": "Execute VEX Code",
   385→        "readOnlyHint": False,
   386→        "destructiveHint": True,
   387→        "idempotentHint": False,
   388→        "openWorldHint": False
   389→    }
   390→}
   391→```
   392→
   393→**Annotation rules:** Use `readOnlyHint: True` for all read/inspect/get operations. Use `destructiveHint: True` for anything that modifies the scene. Use `idempotentHint: True` for set operations where repeat calls produce the same result. MCP clients use these for UI gating and safety decisions.
   394→
   395→#### Tool Dispatch — Bridge to Handlers
   396→
   397→```python
   398→async def dispatch_tool(tool_name: str, arguments: dict) -> dict:
   399→    """Bridge MCP tools/call to existing SYNAPSE handlers.
   400→    Safety middleware is enforced by the handlers — NOT bypassed."""
   401→    handler = HANDLER_REGISTRY.get(tool_name)
   402→    if not handler:
   403→        raise MCPError(-32602, f"Unknown tool: {tool_name}")
   404→    try:
   405→        result = await handler(arguments)
   406→        return {
   407→            "content": [{"type": "text", "text": json.dumps(result) if isinstance(result, dict) else str(result)}]
   408→        }
   409→    except SynapseError as e:
   410→        return {"content": [{"type": "text", "text": f"Error: {e.message}"}], "isError": True}
   411→```
   412→
   413→**CRITICAL:** `dispatch_tool` implements zero safety logic. It delegates to existing handlers which already enforce atomic scripts, idempotent guards, and undo-group transactions. The MCP layer is a thin protocol translation.

   491→#### Security
   492→
   493→- **Localhost binding only** by default (`127.0.0.1`, not `0.0.0.0`). Claude Code runs locally.
   494→- **No auth for local** — MCP spec permits authless localhost. Bearer token auth is opt-in (Phase 3) for remote/studio deployment.
   495→- **Origin validation** — validate `Origin` header per MCP spec to mitigate DNS rebinding.
   496→- **Cloud context awareness** — Claude Code sends tool results to Anthropic's API. Scene data (node names, attribute values) transits cloud infrastructure. Document this for users with proprietary scenes.
   497→
   498→#### SDK vs. Manual Implementation
   499→
   500→Two approaches available:
   501→
   502→**Option A — Python MCP SDK (`pip install mcp`):** Handles all protocol plumbing (JSON-RPC, sessions, capabilities). Use `from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP` with `@mcp.tool()` decorators. Trade-off: introduces an external dependency and its own HTTP server — evaluate whether it integrates cleanly with hwebserver or conflicts.
   503→
   504→**Option B — Manual implementation:** Build the JSON-RPC router directly on hwebserver. More control, zero new dependencies, but more boilerplate.
   505→
   506→**Recommended:** Try the SDK first. If hwebserver integration is clean, use it. If not, fall back to manual. Either way, the dispatch layer delegates to existing handlers — the protocol plumbing is the only variable.

   518→## Testing Patterns
   519→
   520→**No Houdini required**: All tests import modules via `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location`, bypassing the `hou` dependency. There is no shared `conftest.py` — each test file creates its own minimal `hou` stub inline via `sys.modules["hou"] = mock_hou`. Some test files (e.g., `test_guards.py`, `test_keyframe_aov.py`) save and restore the original `sys.modules["hou"]` in teardown to prevent cross-test pollution.
   521→
   522→**Patching `hou` in handler tests**: Always patch the module-level reference inside handlers.py, NOT `sys.modules["hou"]`. Patching sys.modules breaks object identity across test files.
   523→
   524→```python
   525→# Correct — patch the handlers module's hou reference
   526→_handlers_hou = handlers_mod.hou
   527→with patch.object(_handlers_hou, "node", return_value=mock_node):
   528→    ...
   529→
   530→# For attributes missing from the stub
   531→with patch.object(hou, "flipbook", create=True):
   532→    ...
   533→```
   534→
   535→**test_guards.py ordering**: Replaces `sys.modules["hou"]` entirely — has save/restore teardown to prevent pollution. `test_render.py` captures `_handlers_hou = handlers_mod.hou` to patch the correct object.
   536→
   537→**Error assertions**: Use `"Couldn't find"` (not `"not found"`) — matches coaching tone convention.
   538→
   539→**Windows encoding**: Any test writing files with em-dashes or special chars must use `encoding="utf-8"` (cp1252 breaks).
   540→
   541→**MCP protocol tests**: Test the JSON-RPC router, session management, tool dispatch, and resource reading without Houdini. Mock the handler registry to return canned responses. Verify correct error codes, header handling (`Mcp-Session-Id`, `MCP-Protocol-Version`), and content-type negotiation. Follow the same stub pattern as existing tests.

   543→## Adding New Functionality
   544→
   545→### Adding a new MCP tool
   546→
   547→1. Add `CommandType` variant in `core/protocol.py`
   548→2. Add handler method `_handle_<name>` in `server/handlers.py` and register it in `SynapseHandler._register_handlers()`
   549→3. Add parameter aliases in `core/aliases.py` if the tool has new parameter names
   550→4. Add `Tool(...)` entry to `list_tools()` and dispatch case to `call_tool()` in `mcp_server.py` (uses `Server.list_tools()`/`Server.call_tool()` decorators, not `@mcp.tool()` decorator pattern). All 38 tools defined in one `list_tools()` function with a single `call_tool()` switch
   551→5. **Add MCP tool definition in `mcp/tools.py`** — include `inputSchema` (JSON Schema for arguments) and `annotations` (`readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint`, `openWorldHint`). The tool dispatches to the same handler registered in step 2.
   552→6. Add timeout override to `_SLOW_COMMANDS` in `mcp_server.py` if >10s expected
   553→7. Write tests — bootstrap a `hou` stub inline via `sys.modules`, import handlers via `importlib`, patch `_handlers_hou` (not `sys.modules["hou"]`). **Also write a test in `test_mcp_protocol.py`** verifying the tool appears in `tools/list` and `tools/call` dispatches correctly.
   554→
   555→**Going forward, steps 5 and 7 (MCP registration + MCP test) are mandatory for all new tools.** The MCP tool registry is now the standard way to expose SYNAPSE functionality to external clients.

   557→### Adding a routing recipe
   558→
   559→Add to `routing/recipes.py` in the `_register_builtins()` method. 21 recipes (11 basic + 10 production). Recipes are Tier 0.5 — pattern-matched before regex, return multi-step command sequences. For complex workflows, use `execute_python` steps. For dynamic composition with modifiers ("set up X with Y and Z"), add workflow templates to `routing/planner.py`.

   563→Add/edit files in `rag/skills/houdini21-reference/*.md` (26 files, ~3,900 lines). Update topic triggers in `rag/documentation/_metadata/semantic_index.json` (28 topics, 400+ triggers).

   565→## Key Conventions
   566→
   567→**Coaching tone**: Error messages say "Couldn't find node" not "Node not found". Always offer next step. `_suggest_parms(node, name)` provides substring-matched alternatives. See `TONE.md` for the full voice guide.
   568→
   569→**He2025 determinism**: `round_float()` for OUTPUT only — never internal timing. `sort_keys=True` in all JSON serialization (both stdlib `json.dumps` and `orjson.OPT_SORT_KEYS`). `@deterministic` decorator auto-rounds float args. `kahan_sum()` for stable aggregation. Content-based UUIDs via `deterministic_uuid()`. Epoch-based adaptation uses fixed epoch SIZE (not time-based) per He2025.
   570→
   571→**Lazy loading**: `__init__.py` uses `__getattr__` to defer routing/server/UI imports. Optional deps use try/except with `*_AVAILABLE` flags. Keeps Houdini startup fast.
   572→
   573→**Thread safety**: `ReadWriteLock` (writer-priority) in `MemoryStore`. `threading.Lock()` for tier-pin cache. `threading.Event()` for background store loading. `_log_executor` ThreadPoolExecutor(2) for fire-and-forget memory logging.
   574→
   575→**Backwards compat**: All legacy names preserved — `NexusServer`, `EngramMemory`, `HyphaeAuditLog`, etc. Storage auto-migrates from `.nexus/`/`.engram/` to `.synapse/`.
   576→
   577→**Singletons**: `AuditLog`, `HumanGate`, `SynapseBridge`, `CryptoEngine` — accessed via `audit_log()`, `human_gate()`, `get_bridge()`, `get_crypto()`.
   578→
   579→**Error classification**: User errors (`ValueError`, `KeyError`, `AttributeError`, `TypeError`, `IndexError`, `NameError`) do NOT trip circuit breaker. Service errors (`TimeoutError`, threading errors, Houdini crashes) DO trip it.
   580→
   581→**Rollback errors in execute_python**: `_ROLLBACK_ERRORS = (NameError, SyntaxError, TypeError, AttributeError, IndexError)` trigger auto-undo. Operational errors (RuntimeError, hou.OperationFailed) do NOT — earlier mutations may be valid.
   582→
   583→## Lighting Law (Critical Domain Knowledge)
   584→
   585→**Intensity is ALWAYS 1.0 (or below)**. Brightness is controlled by **exposure** (logarithmic, in stops). This applies to ALL PBR renderers (Karma, Arnold, RenderMan, V-Ray).
   586→
   587→- Key:fill ratio 3:1 = 1.585 stops difference (`log2(3)`)
   588→- Key:fill ratio 4:1 = 2.0 stops difference (`log2(4)`)
   589→- USD exposure parm: `xn__inputsexposure_vya` (value), `xn__inputsexposure_control_wcb` = `"set"` (enable)
   590→- USD intensity parm: `xn__inputsintensity_i0a` — always 1.0
   591→
   592→## Rendering Guidelines
   593→
   594→When building or rendering Solaris scenes via MCP, follow a progressive validation pipeline — never jump straight to production settings:
   595→
   596→1. **Validate stage first**: After creating geometry, lights, and materials, query the stage to confirm all expected prims exist at correct paths. Use exact prim paths for material assignments (not wildcard patterns like `/**` unless verified).
   597→2. **Test render at low quality**: Start with 256x256 resolution, low pixel samples (4-8), no SSS, no displacement, no denoiser. Confirm the render completes and produces output before scaling up.
   598→3. **Scale incrementally**: Increase resolution and samples in steps. Enable expensive features (SSS, subsurface scattering, denoiser) one at a time.
   599→4. **Never use foreground rendering for heavy scenes**: `soho_foreground=1` blocks Houdini entirely — if the render is slow, the WebSocket server becomes unresponsive and the user must force-kill Houdini.
   600→5. **Verify output paths**: Set `picture` on the Karma LOP AND `outputimage` on the ROP. Check the output directory exists. Use `iconvert.exe` from `$HFS/bin/` for EXR-to-JPEG conversion.
   601→
   602→## Wire Protocol
   603→
   604→Default: `ws://localhost:9999/synapse` | Version: `4.0.0`
   605→MCP endpoint: `http://localhost:PORT/mcp` | Protocol: MCP 2025-06-18 (Streamable HTTP)
   606→
   607→39 registered handlers: `ping`, `get_health`, `get_help`, `create_node`, `delete_node`, `connect_nodes`, `get_parm`, `set_parm`, `get_scene_info`, `get_selection`, `execute_python`, `execute_vex`, `get_stage_info`, `get_usd_attribute`, `set_usd_attribute`, `create_usd_prim`, `modify_usd_prim`, `capture_viewport`, `render`, `wedge`, `reference_usd`, `set_keyframe`, `render_settings`, `create_material`, `assign_material`, `read_material`, `knowledge_lookup`, `inspect_selection`, `inspect_scene`, `inspect_node`, `batch_commands`, `get_metrics`, `router_stats`, `list_recipes`, `context`, `search`, `add_memory`, `decide`, `recall`
   608→
   609→All 39 handlers are accessible through both the WebSocket transport and the MCP Streamable HTTP transport. Parameter names resolve through `aliases.py` (38+ mappings) — e.g., `node`, `path`, `node_path` all resolve to canonical `node`.
   610→
   611→## Storage Layout
   612→
   613→```
   614→$HIP/.synapse/           # Per-project memory
   615→  memory.jsonl           # Append-only log (async write buffer: 2s flush / 50-item cap / atexit flush)
   616→  index.json             # Search indices (by_type, by_tag, by_keyword)
   617→  context.md             # Human-editable shot context
   618→  decisions.md           # Decision log
   619→  tasks.md               # Task history
   620→
   621→~/.synapse/              # Global
   622→  audit/                 # Daily JSONL audit logs (hash-chain, tamper-evident)
   623→  gates/                 # Gate proposals (timestamped, immutable)
   624→  encryption.key         # Auto-generated Fernet key (AES-128-CBC + HMAC-SHA256)
   625→  agent/                 # Autonomous agent SDK (synapse_agent.py entry point)
   626→  design/                # Design tokens, icon generator, Qt styles
   627→  houdini/               # Shelf, panel, callbacks for Houdini integration
   628→  install.py             # Houdini prefs installer
   629→```
   630→
   631→## Gotchas
   632→
   633→- **matlib.cook(force=True)**: MUST cook materiallibrary before `createNode()` on shader child — without cook, internal subnet doesn't exist and createNode returns None
   634→- **Render output_file kwarg**: Doesn't work for usdrender ROPs — set `outputimage` or `picture` parm directly
   635→- **usdrender loppath**: ROPs in `/out` need `loppath` set to a LOP node — handler auto-discovers display node in `/stage`
   636→- **Karma camera**: Must use USD prim path (`/cameras/render_cam`), not Houdini node path
   637→- **override_res**: String menu `""` / `"scale"` / `"specific"` — not int
   638→- **Viewport capture**: Must use Flipbook API with `hdefereval.executeInMainThreadWithResult()` — `QWidget.grab()` returns black for OpenGL; `executeDeferred()` is fire-and-forget and won't block
   639→- **.pypanel imports**: NEVER nuke `sys.modules` — use `hou.session` guard for one-time import
   640→- **RAG Path import**: Handler uses `from pathlib import Path as _Path` (inline) — global `Path` not available in handlers.py
   641→- **MCP execute_python**: MCP param is `code`, but Synapse handler resolves `content` — payload builder in mcp_server.py maps it
   642→- **SVG icon generation**: XML forbids `--` inside comments; use `|` separator
   643→- **synapse_shelf.py**: Security hooks block `parm.eval()` patterns; use `node.evalParm("parm_name")` method instead
   644→- **Agent SDK websockets**: Must import at module level (not inside connect()) — patch target is `synapse_ws.websockets`
   645→- **Zombie servers**: Multiple SynapseServer instances can linger in Houdini; use `gc.get_objects()` + `_actual_port` to find the active one
   646→- **MCP tool registration (stdio bridge)**: Uses `@server.list_tools()` returning `Tool(...)` list + `@server.call_tool()` dispatcher — NOT the `@mcp.tool()` decorator pattern. All 38 tools defined in one `list_tools()` function with a single `call_tool()` switch
   647→- **MCP tool registration (Streamable HTTP)**: Uses the tool registry in `mcp/tools.py` which maps to the same handlers. Both registries must stay in sync — when adding a tool to `mcp_server.py`, also add it to `mcp/tools.py`
   648→- **MCP session headers**: `Mcp-Session-Id` must be returned on the `initialize` response and included by the client on all subsequent requests. hwebserver header access may require case-insensitive lookup
   649→- **MCP notifications return 202**: `notifications/initialized` and other notification methods return HTTP 202 Accepted with empty body — NOT 200 with a JSON-RPC response
   650→- **MCP protocol version header**: Clients may send `MCP-Protocol-Version` header. If present and unsupported, respond with 400 Bad Request per spec
   651→- **SYNAPSE_PATH env var**: Controls WebSocket path segment (default `/synapse`). `SYNAPSE_PORT` controls port (default `9999`). Full URL: `ws://localhost:{SYNAPSE_PORT}{SYNAPSE_PATH}`
   652→- **orjson optional**: `protocol.py` and `mcp_server.py` use `orjson` for fast JSON with `OPT_SORT_KEYS` when installed, auto-fallback to stdlib `json`
