> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://code.claude.com/docs/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Automate workflows with hooks

> Run shell commands automatically when Claude Code edits files, finishes tasks, or needs input. Format code, send notifications, validate commands, and enforce project rules.

Hooks are user-defined shell commands that execute at specific points in Claude Code's lifecycle. They provide deterministic control over Claude Code's behavior, ensuring certain actions always happen rather than relying on the LLM to choose to run them. Use hooks to enforce project rules, automate repetitive tasks, and integrate Claude Code with your existing tools.

For decisions that require judgment rather than deterministic rules, you can also use [prompt-based hooks](#prompt-based-hooks) or [agent-based hooks](#agent-based-hooks) that use a Claude model to evaluate conditions.

For other ways to extend Claude Code, see [skills](/en/skills) for giving Claude additional instructions and executable commands, [subagents](/en/sub-agents) for running tasks in isolated contexts, and [plugins](/en/plugins) for packaging extensions to share across projects.

<Tip>
  This guide covers common use cases and how to get started. For full event schemas, JSON input/output formats, and advanced features like async hooks and MCP tool hooks, see the [Hooks reference](/en/hooks).
</Tip>

## Set up your first hook

The fastest way to create a hook is through the `/hooks` interactive menu in Claude Code. This walkthrough creates a desktop notification hook, so you get alerted whenever Claude is waiting for your input instead of watching the terminal.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open the hooks menu">
    Type `/hooks` in the Claude Code CLI. You'll see a list of all available hook events, plus an option to disable all hooks. Each event corresponds to a point in Claude's lifecycle where you can run custom code. Select `Notification` to create a hook that fires when Claude needs your attention.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Configure the matcher">
    The menu shows a list of matchers, which filter when the hook fires. Set the matcher to `*` to fire on all notification types. You can narrow it later by changing the matcher to a specific value like `permission_prompt` or `idle_prompt`.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Add your command">
    Select `+ Add new hook…`. The menu prompts you for a shell command to run when the event fires. Hooks run any shell command you provide, so you can use your platform's built-in notification tool. Copy the command for your OS:

    <Tabs>
      <Tab title="macOS">
        Uses [`osascript`](https://ss64.com/mac/osascript.html) to trigger a native macOS notification through AppleScript:

        ```
        osascript -e 'display notification "Claude Code needs your attention" with title "Claude Code"'
        ```
      </Tab>

      <Tab title="Linux">
        Uses `notify-send`, which is pre-installed on most Linux desktops with a notification daemon:

        ```
        notify-send 'Claude Code' 'Claude Code needs your attention'
        ```
      </Tab>

      <Tab title="Windows (PowerShell)">
        Uses PowerShell to show a native message box through .NET's Windows Forms:

        ```
        powershell.exe -Command "[System.Reflection.Assembly]::LoadWithPartialName('System.Windows.Forms'); [System.Windows.Forms.MessageBox]::Show('Claude Code needs your attention', 'Claude Code')"
        ```
      </Tab>
    </Tabs>
  </Step>

  <Step title="Choose a storage location">
    The menu asks where to save the hook configuration. Select `User settings` to store it in `~/.claude/settings.json`, which applies the hook to all your projects. You could also choose `Project settings` to scope it to the current project. See [Configure hook location](#configure-hook-location) for all available scopes.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Test the hook">
    Press `Esc` to return to the CLI. Ask Claude to do something that requires permission, then switch away from the terminal. You should receive a desktop notification.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## What you can automate

Hooks let you run code at key points in Claude Code's lifecycle: format files after edits, block commands before they execute, send notifications when Claude needs input, inject context at session start, and more. For the full list of hook events, see the [Hooks reference](/en/hooks#hook-lifecycle).

Each example includes a ready-to-use configuration block that you add to a [settings file](#configure-hook-location). The most common patterns:

* [Get notified when Claude needs input](#get-notified-when-claude-needs-input)
* [Auto-format code after edits](#auto-format-code-after-edits)
* [Block edits to protected files](#block-edits-to-protected-files)
* [Re-inject context after compaction](#re-inject-context-after-compaction)

### Get notified when Claude needs input

Get a desktop notification whenever Claude finishes working and needs your input, so you can switch to other tasks without checking the terminal.

This hook uses the `Notification` event, which fires when Claude is waiting for input or permission. Each tab below uses the platform's native notification command. Add this to `~/.claude/settings.json`, or use the [interactive walkthrough](#set-up-your-first-hook) above to configure it with `/hooks`:

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="macOS">
    ```json  theme={null}
    {
      "hooks": {
        "Notification": [
          {
            "matcher": "",
            "hooks": [
              {
                "type": "command",
                "command": "osascript -e 'display notification \"Claude Code needs your attention\" with title \"Claude Code\"'"
              }
            ]
          }
        ]
      }
    }
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Linux">
    ```json  theme={null}
    {
      "hooks": {
        "Notification": [
          {
            "matcher": "",
            "hooks": [
              {
                "type": "command",
                "command": "notify-send 'Claude Code' 'Claude Code needs your attention'"
              }
            ]
          }
        ]
      }
    }
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Windows (PowerShell)">
    ```json  theme={null}
    {
      "hooks": {
        "Notification": [
          {
            "matcher": "",
            "hooks": [
              {
                "type": "command",
                "command": "powershell.exe -Command \"[System.Reflection.Assembly]::LoadWithPartialName('System.Windows.Forms'); [System.Windows.Forms.MessageBox]::Show('Claude Code needs your attention', 'Claude Code')\""
              }
            ]
          }
        ]
      }
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

### Auto-format code after edits

Automatically run [Prettier](https://prettier.io/) on every file Claude edits, so formatting stays consistent without manual intervention.

This hook uses the `PostToolUse` event with an `Edit|Write` matcher, so it runs only after file-editing tools. The command extracts the edited file path with [`jq`](https://jqlang.github.io/jq/) and passes it to Prettier. Add this to `.claude/settings.json` in your project root:

```json  theme={null}
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [
      {
        "matcher": "Edit|Write",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "jq -r '.tool_input.file_path' | xargs npx prettier --write"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

<Note>
  The Bash examples on this page use `jq` for JSON parsing. Install it with `brew install jq` (macOS), `apt-get install jq` (Debian/Ubuntu), or see [`jq` downloads](https://jqlang.github.io/jq/download/).
</Note>

### Block edits to protected files

Prevent Claude from modifying sensitive files like `.env`, `package-lock.json`, or anything in `.git/`. Claude receives feedback explaining why the edit was blocked, so it can adjust its approach.

This example uses a separate script file that the hook calls. The script checks the target file path against a list of protected patterns and exits with code 2 to block the edit.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Create the hook script">
    Save this to `.claude/hooks/protect-files.sh`:

    ```bash  theme={null}
    #!/bin/bash
    # protect-files.sh

    INPUT=$(cat)
    FILE_PATH=$(echo "$INPUT" | jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // empty')

    PROTECTED_PATTERNS=(".env" "package-lock.json" ".git/")

    for pattern in "${PROTECTED_PATTERNS[@]}"; do
      if [[ "$FILE_PATH" == *"$pattern"* ]]; then
        echo "Blocked: $FILE_PATH matches protected pattern '$pattern'" >&2
        exit 2
      fi
    done

    exit 0
    ```
  </Step>

  <Step title="Make the script executable (macOS/Linux)">
    Hook scripts must be executable for Claude Code to run them:

    ```bash  theme={null}
    chmod +x .claude/hooks/protect-files.sh
    ```
  </Step>

  <Step title="Register the hook">
    Add a `PreToolUse` hook to `.claude/settings.json` that runs the script before any `Edit` or `Write` tool call:

    ```json  theme={null}
    {
      "hooks": {
        "PreToolUse": [
          {
            "matcher": "Edit|Write",
            "hooks": [
              {
                "type": "command",
                "command": "\"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\"/.claude/hooks/protect-files.sh"
              }
            ]
          }
        ]
      }
    }
    ```
  </Step>
</Steps>

### Re-inject context after compaction

When Claude's context window fills up, compaction summarizes the conversation to free space. This can lose important details. Use a `SessionStart` hook with a `compact` matcher to re-inject critical context after every compaction.

Any text your command writes to stdout is added to Claude's context. This example reminds Claude of project conventions and recent work. Add this to `.claude/settings.json` in your project root:

```json  theme={null}
{
  "hooks": {
    "SessionStart": [
      {
        "matcher": "compact",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "echo 'Reminder: use Bun, not npm. Run bun test before committing. Current sprint: auth refactor.'"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

You can replace the `echo` with any command that produces dynamic output, like `git log --oneline -5` to show recent commits. For injecting context on every session start, consider using [CLAUDE.md](/en/memory) instead. For environment variables, see [`CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`](/en/hooks#persist-environment-variables) in the reference.

## How hooks work

Hook events fire at specific lifecycle points in Claude Code. When an event fires, all matching hooks run in parallel, and identical hook commands are automatically deduplicated. The table below shows each event and when it triggers:

| Event                | When it fires                                                      |
| :------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SessionStart`       | When a session begins or resumes                                   |
| `UserPromptSubmit`   | When you submit a prompt, before Claude processes it               |
| `PreToolUse`         | Before a tool call executes. Can block it                          |
| `PermissionRequest`  | When a permission dialog appears                                   |
| `PostToolUse`        | After a tool call succeeds                                         |
| `PostToolUseFailure` | After a tool call fails                                            |
| `Notification`       | When Claude Code sends a notification                              |
| `SubagentStart`      | When a subagent is spawned                                         |
| `SubagentStop`       | When a subagent finishes                                           |
| `Stop`               | When Claude finishes responding                                    |
| `TeammateIdle`       | When an [agent team](/en/agent-teams) teammate is about to go idle |
| `TaskCompleted`      | When a task is being marked as completed                           |
| `PreCompact`         | Before context compaction                                          |
| `SessionEnd`         | When a session terminates                                          |

Each hook has a `type` that determines how it runs. Most hooks use `"type": "command"`, which runs a shell command. Two other options use a Claude model to make decisions: `"type": "prompt"` for single-turn evaluation and `"type": "agent"` for multi-turn verification with tool access. See [Prompt-based hooks](#prompt-based-hooks) and [Agent-based hooks](#agent-based-hooks) for details.

### Read input and return output

Hooks communicate with Claude Code through stdin, stdout, stderr, and exit codes. When an event fires, Claude Code passes event-specific data as JSON to your script's stdin. Your script reads that data, does its work, and tells Claude Code what to do next via the exit code.

#### Hook input

Every event includes common fields like `session_id` and `cwd`, but each event type adds different data. For example, when Claude runs a Bash command, a `PreToolUse` hook receives something like this on stdin:

```json  theme={null}
{
  "session_id": "abc123",          // unique ID for this session
  "cwd": "/Users/sarah/myproject", // working directory when the event fired
  "hook_event_name": "PreToolUse", // which event triggered this hook
  "tool_name": "Bash",             // the tool Claude is about to use
  "tool_input": {                  // the arguments Claude passed to the tool
    "command": "npm test"          // for Bash, this is the shell command
  }
}
```

Your script can parse that JSON and act on any of those fields. `UserPromptSubmit` hooks get the `prompt` text instead, `SessionStart` hooks get the `source` (startup, resume, compact), and so on. See [Common input fields](/en/hooks#common-input-fields) in the reference for shared fields, and each event's section for event-specific schemas.

#### Hook output

Your script tells Claude Code what to do next by writing to stdout or stderr and exiting with a specific code. For example, a `PreToolUse` hook that wants to block a command:

```bash  theme={null}
#!/bin/bash
INPUT=$(cat)
COMMAND=$(echo "$INPUT" | jq -r '.tool_input.command')

if echo "$COMMAND" | grep -q "drop table"; then
  echo "Blocked: dropping tables is not allowed" >&2  # stderr becomes Claude's feedback
  exit 2                                               # exit 2 = block the action
fi

exit 0  # exit 0 = let it proceed
```

The exit code determines what happens next:

* **Exit 0**: the action proceeds. For `UserPromptSubmit` and `SessionStart` hooks, anything you write to stdout is added to Claude's context.
* **Exit 2**: the action is blocked. Write a reason to stderr, and Claude receives it as feedback so it can adjust.
* **Any other exit code**: the action proceeds. Stderr is logged but not shown to Claude. Toggle verbose mode with `Ctrl+O` to see these messages in the transcript.

#### Structured JSON output

Exit codes give you two options: allow or block. For more control, exit 0 and print a JSON object to stdout instead.

<Note>
  Use exit 2 to block with a stderr message, or exit 0 with JSON for structured control. Don't mix them: Claude Code ignores JSON when you exit 2.
</Note>

For example, a `PreToolUse` hook can deny a tool call and tell Claude why, or escalate it to the user for approval:

```json  theme={null}
{
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
    "permissionDecision": "deny",
    "permissionDecisionReason": "Use rg instead of grep for better performance"
  }
}
```

Claude Code reads `permissionDecision` and cancels the tool call, then feeds `permissionDecisionReason` back to Claude as feedback. These three options are specific to `PreToolUse`:

* `"allow"`: proceed without showing a permission prompt
* `"deny"`: cancel the tool call and send the reason to Claude
* `"ask"`: show the permission prompt to the user as normal

Other events use different decision patterns. For example, `PostToolUse` and `Stop` hooks use a top-level `decision: "block"` field, while `PermissionRequest` uses `hookSpecificOutput.decision.behavior`. See the [summary table](/en/hooks#decision-control) in the reference for a full breakdown by event.

For `UserPromptSubmit` hooks, use `additionalContext` instead to inject text into Claude's context. Prompt-based hooks (`type: "prompt"`) handle output differently: see [Prompt-based hooks](#prompt-based-hooks).

### Filter hooks with matchers

Without a matcher, a hook fires on every occurrence of its event. Matchers let you narrow that down. For example, if you want to run a formatter only after file edits (not after every tool call), add a matcher to your `PostToolUse` hook:

```json  theme={null}
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [
      {
        "matcher": "Edit|Write",
        "hooks": [
          { "type": "command", "command": "prettier --write ..." }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

The `"Edit|Write"` matcher is a regex pattern that matches the tool name. The hook only fires when Claude uses the `Edit` or `Write` tool, not when it uses `Bash`, `Read`, or any other tool.

Each event type matches on a specific field. Matchers support exact strings and regex patterns:

| Event                                                                  | What the matcher filters  | Example matcher values                                                         |
| :--------------------------------------------------------------------- | :------------------------ | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`, `PermissionRequest` | tool name                 | `Bash`, `Edit\|Write`, `mcp__.*`                                               |
| `SessionStart`                                                         | how the session started   | `startup`, `resume`, `clear`, `compact`                                        |
| `SessionEnd`                                                           | why the session ended     | `clear`, `logout`, `prompt_input_exit`, `bypass_permissions_disabled`, `other` |
| `Notification`                                                         | notification type         | `permission_prompt`, `idle_prompt`, `auth_success`, `elicitation_dialog`       |
| `SubagentStart`                                                        | agent type                | `Bash`, `Explore`, `Plan`, or custom agent names                               |
| `PreCompact`                                                           | what triggered compaction | `manual`, `auto`                                                               |
| `UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop`, `TeammateIdle`, `TaskCompleted`            | no matcher support        | always fires on every occurrence                                               |
| `SubagentStop`                                                         | agent type                | same values as `SubagentStart`                                                 |

A few more examples showing matchers on different event types:

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Log every Bash command">
    Match only `Bash` tool calls and log each command to a file. The `PostToolUse` event fires after the command completes, so `tool_input.command` contains what ran. The hook receives the event data as JSON on stdin, and `jq -r '.tool_input.command'` extracts just the command string, which `>>` appends to the log file:

    ```json  theme={null}
    {
      "hooks": {
        "PostToolUse": [
          {
            "matcher": "Bash",
            "hooks": [
              {
                "type": "command",
                "command": "jq -r '.tool_input.command' >> ~/.claude/command-log.txt"
              }
            ]
          }
        ]
      }
    }
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Match MCP tools">
    MCP tools use a different naming convention than built-in tools: `mcp__<server>__<tool>`, where `<server>` is the MCP server name and `<tool>` is the tool it provides. For example, `mcp__github__search_repositories` or `mcp__filesystem__read_file`. Use a regex matcher to target all tools from a specific server, or match across servers with a pattern like `mcp__.*__write.*`. See [Match MCP tools](/en/hooks#match-mcp-tools) in the reference for the full list of examples.

    The command below extracts the tool name from the hook's JSON input with `jq` and writes it to stderr, where it shows up in verbose mode (`Ctrl+O`):

    ```json  theme={null}
    {
      "hooks": {
        "PreToolUse": [
          {
            "matcher": "mcp__github__.*",
            "hooks": [
              {
                "type": "command",
                "command": "echo \"GitHub tool called: $(jq -r '.tool_name')\" >&2"
              }
            ]
          }
        ]
      }
    }
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Clean up on session end">
    The `SessionEnd` event supports matchers on the reason the session ended. This hook only fires on `clear` (when you run `/clear`), not on normal exits:

    ```json  theme={null}
    {
      "hooks": {
        "SessionEnd": [
          {
            "matcher": "clear",
            "hooks": [
              {
                "type": "command",
                "command": "rm -f /tmp/claude-scratch-*.txt"
              }
            ]
          }
        ]
      }
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

For full matcher syntax, see the [Hooks reference](/en/hooks#configuration).

### Configure hook location

Where you add a hook determines its scope:

| Location                                                   | Scope                              | Shareable                          |
| :--------------------------------------------------------- | :--------------------------------- | :--------------------------------- |
| `~/.claude/settings.json`                                  | All your projects                  | No, local to your machine          |
| `.claude/settings.json`                                    | Single project                     | Yes, can be committed to the repo  |
| `.claude/settings.local.json`                              | Single project                     | No, gitignored                     |
| Managed policy settings                                    | Organization-wide                  | Yes, admin-controlled              |
| [Plugin](/en/plugins) `hooks/hooks.json`                   | When plugin is enabled             | Yes, bundled with the plugin       |
| [Skill](/en/skills) or [agent](/en/sub-agents) frontmatter | While the skill or agent is active | Yes, defined in the component file |

You can also use the [`/hooks` menu](/en/hooks#the-hooks-menu) in Claude Code to add, delete, and view hooks interactively. To disable all hooks at once, use the toggle at the bottom of the `/hooks` menu or set `"disableAllHooks": true` in your settings file.

Hooks added through the `/hooks` menu take effect immediately. If you edit settings files directly while Claude Code is running, the changes won't take effect until you review them in the `/hooks` menu or restart your session.

## Prompt-based hooks

For decisions that require judgment rather than deterministic rules, use `type: "prompt"` hooks. Instead of running a shell command, Claude Code sends your prompt and the hook's input data to a Claude model (Haiku by default) to make the decision. You can specify a different model with the `model` field if you need more capability.

The model's only job is to return a yes/no decision as JSON:

* `"ok": true`: the action proceeds
* `"ok": false`: the action is blocked. The model's `"reason"` is fed back to Claude so it can adjust.

This example uses a `Stop` hook to ask the model whether all requested tasks are complete. If the model returns `"ok": false`, Claude keeps working and uses the `reason` as its next instruction:

```json  theme={null}
{
  "hooks": {
    "Stop": [
      {
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "prompt",
            "prompt": "Check if all tasks are complete. If not, respond with {\"ok\": false, \"reason\": \"what remains to be done\"}."
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

For full configuration options, see [Prompt-based hooks](/en/hooks#prompt-based-hooks) in the reference.

## Agent-based hooks

When verification requires inspecting files or running commands, use `type: "agent"` hooks. Unlike prompt hooks which make a single LLM call, agent hooks spawn a subagent that can read files, search code, and use other tools to verify conditions before returning a decision.

Agent hooks use the same `"ok"` / `"reason"` response format as prompt hooks, but with a longer default timeout of 60 seconds and up to 50 tool-use turns.

This example verifies that tests pass before allowing Claude to stop:

```json  theme={null}
{
  "hooks": {
    "Stop": [
      {
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "agent",
            "prompt": "Verify that all unit tests pass. Run the test suite and check the results. $ARGUMENTS",
            "timeout": 120
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Use prompt hooks when the hook input data alone is enough to make a decision. Use agent hooks when you need to verify something against the actual state of the codebase.

For full configuration options, see [Agent-based hooks](/en/hooks#agent-based-hooks) in the reference.

## Limitations and troubleshooting

### Limitations

* Hooks communicate through stdout, stderr, and exit codes only. They cannot trigger slash commands or tool calls directly.
* Hook timeout is 10 minutes by default, configurable per hook with the `timeout` field (in seconds).
* `PostToolUse` hooks cannot undo actions since the tool has already executed.
* `PermissionRequest` hooks do not fire in [non-interactive mode](/en/headless) (`-p`). Use `PreToolUse` hooks for automated permission decisions.
* `Stop` hooks fire whenever Claude finishes responding, not only at task completion. They do not fire on user interrupts.

### Hook not firing

The hook is configured but never executes.

* Run `/hooks` and confirm the hook appears under the correct event
* Check that the matcher pattern matches the tool name exactly (matchers are case-sensitive)
* Verify you're triggering the right event type (e.g., `PreToolUse` fires before tool execution, `PostToolUse` fires after)
* If using `PermissionRequest` hooks in non-interactive mode (`-p`), switch to `PreToolUse` instead

### Hook error in output

You see a message like "PreToolUse hook error: ..." in the transcript.

* Your script exited with a non-zero code unexpectedly. Test it manually by piping sample JSON:
  ```bash  theme={null}
  echo '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"ls"}}' | ./my-hook.sh
  echo $?  # Check the exit code
  ```
* If you see "command not found", use absolute paths or `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` to reference scripts
* If you see "jq: command not found", install `jq` or use Python/Node.js for JSON parsing
* If the script isn't running at all, make it executable: `chmod +x ./my-hook.sh`

### `/hooks` shows no hooks configured

You edited a settings file but the hooks don't appear in the menu.

* Restart your session or open `/hooks` to reload. Hooks added through the `/hooks` menu take effect immediately, but manual file edits require a reload.
* Verify your JSON is valid (trailing commas and comments are not allowed)
* Confirm the settings file is in the correct location: `.claude/settings.json` for project hooks, `~/.claude/settings.json` for global hooks

### Stop hook runs forever

Claude keeps working in an infinite loop instead of stopping.

Your Stop hook script needs to check whether it already triggered a continuation. Parse the `stop_hook_active` field from the JSON input and exit early if it's `true`:

```bash  theme={null}
#!/bin/bash
INPUT=$(cat)
if [ "$(echo "$INPUT" | jq -r '.stop_hook_active')" = "true" ]; then
  exit 0  # Allow Claude to stop
fi
# ... rest of your hook logic
```

### JSON validation failed

Claude Code shows a JSON parsing error even though your hook script outputs valid JSON.

When Claude Code runs a hook, it spawns a shell that sources your profile (`~/.zshrc` or `~/.bashrc`). If your profile contains unconditional `echo` statements, that output gets prepended to your hook's JSON:

```
Shell ready on arm64
{"decision": "block", "reason": "Not allowed"}
```

Claude Code tries to parse this as JSON and fails. To fix this, wrap echo statements in your shell profile so they only run in interactive shells:

```bash  theme={null}
# In ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc
if [[ $- == *i* ]]; then
  echo "Shell ready"
fi
```

The `$-` variable contains shell flags, and `i` means interactive. Hooks run in non-interactive shells, so the echo is skipped.

### Debug techniques

Toggle verbose mode with `Ctrl+O` to see hook output in the transcript, or run `claude --debug` for full execution details including which hooks matched and their exit codes.

## Learn more

* [Hooks reference](/en/hooks): full event schemas, JSON output format, async hooks, and MCP tool hooks
* [Security considerations](/en/hooks#security-considerations): review before deploying hooks in shared or production environments

## Claude Code Hooks: Complete Reference

I've pulled the exact specifications from the official Claude Code documentation. Here's what you need to know:

### 1. Settings.json Hooks Configuration Structure

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [
      {
        "matcher": "Edit|Write",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": ".claude/hooks/your-script.sh",
            "timeout": 600
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

**Hook locations (scope levels):**
- `~/.claude/settings.json` — all your projects
- `.claude/settings.json` — single project (shareable via git)
- `.claude/settings.local.json` — single project (gitignored)

### 2. PreToolUse Hook Input (stdin JSON Schema)

For **Edit** and **Write** tools specifically:

#### Write Tool Input
```json
{
  "session_id": "abc123",
  "transcript_path": "/Users/.../transcript.jsonl",
  "cwd": "/Users/...",
  "permission_mode": "default",
  "hook_event_name": "PreToolUse",
  "tool_name": "Write",
  "tool_input": {
    "file_path": "/path/to/file.txt",
    "content": "file content here"
  },
  "tool_use_id": "toolu_01ABC123..."
}
```

#### Edit Tool Input
```json
{
  "session_id": "abc123",
  "transcript_path": "/Users/.../transcript.jsonl",
  "cwd": "/Users/...",
  "permission_mode": "default",
  "hook_event_name": "PreToolUse",
  "tool_name": "Edit",
  "tool_input": {
    "file_path": "/path/to/file.txt",
    "old_string": "original text",
    "new_string": "replacement text",
    "replace_all": false
  },
  "tool_use_id": "toolu_01ABC123..."
}
```

### 3. How to Block a Tool Call

There are **two patterns** depending on your approach:

#### Pattern A: Exit Code 2 (Blocking Error)
```bash
#!/bin/bash
INPUT=$(cat)
FILE_PATH=$(echo "$INPUT" | jq -r '.tool_input.file_path')

if [[ "$FILE_PATH" == *".env"* ]]; then
  echo "Blocked: Cannot edit .env files" >&2  # stderr
  exit 2  # Blocking error = prevents tool call
fi

exit 0  # Success = allows tool call
```

**Exit code behavior:**
- `exit 0` = allow the action to proceed
- `exit 2` = block the action (stderr text becomes the feedback to Claude)
- Any other code = non-blocking error (stderr shown in verbose mode only)

#### Pattern B: JSON Output with hookSpecificOutput (Structured Control)
```bash
#!/bin/bash
INPUT=$(cat)
FILE_PATH=$(echo "$INPUT" | jq -r '.tool_input.file_path')

if [[ "$FILE_PATH" == *".env"* ]]; then
  jq -n '{
    "hookSpecificOutput": {
      "hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
      "permissionDecision": "deny",
      "permissionDecisionReason": "Cannot edit .env files"
    }
  }'
  exit 0  # Exit 0 when using JSON output
else
  exit 0  # Allow with no JSON output
fi
```

**PreToolUse Decision Values:**
- `"allow"` — bypass permission prompt, proceed directly
- `"deny"` — cancel the tool call
- `"ask"` — show the permission prompt to the user

### 4. How to Show a Message to the User

**When blocking with exit code 2:**
```bash
echo "Your message here" >&2  # stderr is shown to Claude as feedback
exit 2
```

**When using JSON output:**
```json
{
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
    "permissionDecision": "deny",
    "permissionDecisionReason": "Your message is shown to Claude here"
  }
}
```

**For context injection (SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit):**
```json
{
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "SessionStart",
    "additionalContext": "This text is added to Claude's context window"
  }
}
```

### 5. Matcher Format

Matchers are **regex patterns** that filter which tools trigger the hook:

```json
{
  "matcher": "Edit|Write"           // exact: Edit OR Write
}
```

**For tool events (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, etc.):**
- Match on `tool_name` field
- `"Edit"`, `"Write"`, `"Bash"`, `"Read"`, `"Glob"`, `"Grep"`, etc.
- Regex syntax: `"Edit|Write"`, `"mcp__.*"`, `".*python.*"`

**For other events:**
| Event | Matches on | Examples |
|-------|-----------|----------|
| `SessionStart` | session source | `"startup"`, `"resume"`, `"compact"` |
| `SessionEnd` | exit reason | `"clear"`, `"logout"`, `"other"` |
| `Notification` | notification type | `"permission_prompt"`, `"idle_prompt"` |

Omit `matcher` or set to `""` to match all occurrences.

### 6. Complete Real-World Example: Block Protected Files

**.claude/settings.json**
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [
      {
        "matcher": "Edit|Write",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "\"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\"/.claude/hooks/protect-files.sh"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

**.claude/hooks/protect-files.sh**
```bash
#!/bin/bash
INPUT=$(cat)
FILE_PATH=$(echo "$INPUT" | jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // empty')

# Patterns to protect
PROTECTED=(".env" "package-lock.json" ".git/" "secrets.key")

for pattern in "${PROTECTED[@]}"; do
  if [[ "$FILE_PATH" == *"$pattern"* ]]; then
    jq -n '{
      "hookSpecificOutput": {
        "hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
        "permissionDecision": "deny",
        "permissionDecisionReason": "Cannot modify '"$pattern"' files. This is a protected file."
      }
    }'
    exit 0  # Exit 0 when using JSON
  fi
done

exit 0  # Allow by default
```

Make executable: `chmod +x .claude/hooks/protect-files.sh`

### Key Points for Your Config

From your `settings.json`, you're already using this pattern for `PostToolUse`:

```json
"hooks": {
  "PostToolUse": [
    {
      "matcher": "Edit|Write",
      "hooks": [
        {
          "type": "command",
          "command": ".claude/hooks/check-python.sh",
          "timeout": 30
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

For **blocking at Pre-execution** (before tool runs), use `PreToolUse`. For **validation after** (like your Python check), use `PostToolUse`. The stdin JSON is identical structure—the difference is timing.

Sources:
- [Claude Code Hooks Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md)
- [Claude Code Hooks Guide](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide.md)

# Reads hook input JSON from stdin, extracts file_path, runs py_compile

INPUT=$(cat)
FILE_PATH=$(echo "$INPUT" | python -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin).get('tool_input',{}).get('file_path',''))" 2>/dev/null)

if [[ "$FILE_PATH" == *.py ]] && [[ -f "$FILE_PATH" ]]; then
  python -m py_compile "$FILE_PATH" 2>&1 || echo "SYNTAX ERROR in $FILE_PATH"
fi

exit 0

## What item 15 literally proposes

Deploy fails → Claude diagnoses → Claude fixes the code → Claude redeploys → Claude validates. Retry loop, no human in it. On the surface, this is just CI/CD with an LLM in the error-handling path. Jenkins does this. ArgoCD does this. Nothing novel.

```
Claude writes SYNAPSE code

        → deploys it...
```

That **is** a feedback loop. The output of one cycle becomes the input to the next. Each iteration expands the agent's operating envelope.

No — but it's adjacent, and the distinction matters.

**True recursive self-improvement** (the alignment-literature version) means the system modifies its own reasoning to become better at modifying its own reasoning. Unbounded optimization pressure. Intelligence explosion. That requires weight modification or architecture search, neither of which happens here.

What you've built is better described as **recursive capability extension**:

| Property | Recursive Self-Improvement | What you're building |
|----------|---------------------------|---------------------|
| What changes | Core reasoning (weights) | Operating environment (tools, hooks, memory) |
| Optimization target | Unbounded (maximize intelligence) | Fixed (deploy works, tests pass) |
| Feedback loop | Agent improves agent | Agent improves agent's *toolchain* |
| Gatekeeper | None (that's the risk) | You (architectural approval, CLAUDE.md, hooks) |
| Compounding | Exponential (each cycle accelerates) | Linear (each cycle adds capability, not acceleration) |

The model's intelligence is frozen. What grows is the **exoskeleton** — the scaffolding of tools, hooks, memory, and skills that surround it. Claude doesn't get smarter; Claude gets more *equipped*.

Here's what I think your question is really pointing at. Look at your session arc across these two days:

## The honest edge case

Where it gets philosophically interesting: if Claude fixes a bug in SYNAPSE's memory system, and that fix makes Claude's cross-session recall better, and better recall leads to Claude writing better SYNAPSE code... that's a weak compounding effect. Not exponential, not dangerous, but real. The capability curve bends slightly upward with each cycle.

    29→def _suggest_parms(node, invalid_name: str, limit: int = 8) -> str:
    30→    """Find similar parameter names on a node for error enrichment."""
    31→    try:
    32→        all_names = [p.name() for p in node.parms()]
    33→    except Exception:
    34→        return ""
    35→    needle = invalid_name.lower()
    36→    matches = [n for n in all_names if needle in n.lower() or n.lower() in needle]
    37→    if not matches:
    38→        # Fallback: common prefix match
    39→        matches = [n for n in all_names if n.lower().startswith(needle[:3])]
    40→    # Check USD alias -- if the invalid name maps to an encoded USD parm, include hint
    41→    usd_hint = ""
    42→    usd_encoded = USD_PARM_ALIASES.get(invalid_name.lower())
    43→    if usd_encoded and usd_encoded in all_names:
    44→        usd_hint = f" Try '{usd_encoded}' (the encoded USD name for '{invalid_name}')."
    45→    if not matches and not usd_hint:
    46→        return ""
    47→    parts = []
    48→    if usd_hint:
    49→        parts.append(usd_hint)
    50→    if matches:
    51→        parts.append(" Similar parameters: " + ", ".join(matches[:limit]))
    52→    return "".join(parts)
    53→
    54→
    55→def _find_render_rop():
    56→    """Auto-discover a render ROP node. Searches /stage then /out."""
    57→    _RENDER_TYPES = {
    58→        "karma", "karmarendersettings",
    59→        "usdrender", "usdrender_rop",
    60→        "ifd",
    61→        "opengl",
    62→    }
    63→    for parent_path in ["/stage", "/out"]:
    64→        parent = hou.node(parent_path)
    65→        if parent is None:
    66→            continue
    67→        for child in parent.children():
    68→            if child.type().name() in _RENDER_TYPES:
    69→                return child
    70→    raise ValueError(
    71→        "Couldn't auto-find a render ROP -- specify the 'node' parameter "
    72→        "with the path to your ROP (e.g. '/stage/karma1' or '/out/mantra1')"
    73→    )
    74→
    75→
    76→def _detect_karma_engine(node, node_type: str) -> str:
    77→    """Detect Karma XPU vs CPU vs Mantra vs other renderer.
    78→
    79→    Karma XPU is the GPU+CPU hybrid renderer; Karma CPU is pure CPU.
    80→    The engine is selected by a parm on the ROP or Karma Render Settings LOP.
    81→    """
    82→    if node_type == "ifd":
    83→        return "mantra"
    84→    if node_type == "opengl":
    85→        return "opengl"
    86→    if node_type not in ("karma", "karmarendersettings", "usdrender", "usdrender_rop"):
    87→        return node_type
    88→
    89→    # Check common parm names for Karma engine variant
    90→    for parm_name in ("renderer", "karmarenderertype", "renderengine"):
    91→        parm = node.parm(parm_name)
    92→        if parm is not None:
    93→            # hou.Parm.eval() reads the parameter value -- not Python eval()
    94→            val = str(parm.eval()).lower()  # noqa: S307
    95→            if "xpu" in val:
    96→                return "karma_xpu"
    97→            if "cpu" in val:
    98→                return "karma_cpu"
    99→            return f"karma_{val}" if val else "karma"
   100→
   101→    return "karma"
   102→
   103→
   104→_VALIDATE_CHECKS = ("file_integrity", "black_frame", "nan_check",
   105→                     "clipping", "underexposure", "saturation")
   106→
   107→_VALIDATE_DEFAULTS = {

   109→    "clipping_pct": 0.5,

   116→class RenderHandlerMixin:

   118→    wedge, and material handlers."""

   120→    def _handle_capture_viewport(self, payload: Dict) -> Dict:
   121→        """Capture the Houdini viewport as an image file.
   122→
   123→        Uses Houdini's flipbook API for a single-frame capture. This correctly
   124→        reads the OpenGL framebuffer (QWidget.grab() returns black for GL surfaces).
   125→        Must run on the main thread via hdefereval.executeInMainThreadWithResult().
   126→        """

   128→            raise RuntimeError(_HOUDINI_UNAVAILABLE)
   129→
   130→        from pathlib import Path
   131→
   132→        fmt = resolve_param_with_default(payload, "format", "jpeg")
   133→        width = resolve_param_with_default(payload, "width", 800)
   134→        height = resolve_param_with_default(payload, "height", 600)
   135→
   136→        temp_dir = Path(hou.text.expandString("$HOUDINI_TEMP_DIR"))
   137→        ext = "jpg" if fmt == "jpeg" else "png"
   138→        timestamp = int(time.time() * 1000)
   139→        # Flipbook requires $F4 frame pattern in output path

   142→        def _flipbook_on_main_thread():

   147→                raise ValueError(

   149→                    "is open in your current desktop layout"
   150→                )
   151→
   152→            vp = sv.curViewport()
   153→            settings = sv.flipbookSettings()
   154→            cur = int(hou.frame())
   155→            settings.frameRange((cur, cur))
   156→            settings.output(out_pattern)
   157→            settings.useResolution(True)
   158→            settings.resolution((int(width), int(height)))
   159→            sv.flipbook(viewport=vp, settings=settings, open_dialog=False)

   162→            actual = out_pattern.replace("$F4", f"{cur:04d}")

   164→
   165→        import hdefereval

   172→                f"The viewport capture ran but the image wasn't created at {actual_path} -- "
   173→                "this can happen if the viewport is minimized or occluded"
   174→            )
   175→
   176→        return {
   177→            "image_path": actual_path,
   178→            "width": int(width),
   179→            "height": int(height),
   180→            "format": fmt,
   181→        }
   182→
   183→    def _handle_render(self, payload: Dict) -> Dict:
   184→        """Render a frame via Karma, Mantra, or any ROP node.
   185→
   186→        Uses hdefereval.executeInMainThreadWithResult() since hou.RopNode.render()
   187→        must run on Houdini's main thread. Outputs to a temp JPEG for AI preview.
   188→
   189→        Supports Karma XPU (GPU+CPU hybrid), Karma CPU, and Mantra ROPs.
   190→        For Karma nodes, detects and reports the rendering engine variant.
   191→        """
   192→        if not HOU_AVAILABLE:
   193→            raise RuntimeError(_HOUDINI_UNAVAILABLE)
   194→        from pathlib import Path
   195→
   196→        rop_path = resolve_param(payload, "node", required=False)
   197→        frame = resolve_param_with_default(payload, "frame", None)
   198→        width = resolve_param_with_default(payload, "width", None)
   199→        height = resolve_param_with_default(payload, "height", None)
   200→
   201→        def _render_on_main():
   202→            if rop_path:
   203→                node = hou.node(rop_path)
   204→                if node is None:
   205→                    raise ValueError(
   206→                        f"Couldn't find a render ROP at {rop_path} -- "
   207→                        "double-check the path to your ROP node"
   208→                    )
   209→            else:
   210→                node = _find_render_rop()

   212→            # Detect Karma engine variant for metadata
   213→            node_type = node.type().name()
   214→            engine = _detect_karma_engine(node, node_type)
   215→
   216→            # For usdrender ROPs in /out, ensure loppath is set
   217→            lp = node.parm("loppath")
   218→            # hou.Parm.eval() reads parameter value -- not Python eval()
   219→            if lp and not lp.eval():  # noqa: S307

   222→                    lop = hou.node(lop_path)
   223→                    if lop and lop.children():
   224→                        # Find last display node or last child
   225→                        display = [c for c in lop.children() if hasattr(c, 'isDisplayFlagSet') and c.isDisplayFlagSet()]
   226→                        target = display[0] if display else lop.children()[-1]
   227→                        lp.set(target.path())
   228→                        break
   229→
   230→            # Output to temp JPEG (AI preview, not final EXR)
   231→            temp_dir = Path(hou.text.expandString("$HOUDINI_TEMP_DIR"))
   232→            timestamp = int(time.time() * 1000)
   233→            out_path = str(temp_dir / f"synapse_render_{timestamp}.jpg")
   234→
   235→            cur = int(hou.frame()) if frame is None else int(frame)
   236→
   237→            # Resolution override -- res= is a scale factor, so set parms directly
   238→            if width and height:
   239→                w, h = int(width), int(height)
   240→                for rx, ry in [("resolutionx", "resolutiony"), ("res_user1", "res_user2")]:
   241→                    if node.parm(rx):
   242→                        node.parm(rx).set(w)
   243→                        node.parm(ry).set(h)
   244→                        break
   245→                # Enable override if available (usdrender string menu)
   246→                ov = node.parm("override_res")
   247→                # hou.Parm.eval() reads parameter value -- not Python eval()
   248→                if ov and ov.eval() != "specific":  # noqa: S307
   249→                    ov.set("specific")
   250→
   251→            # Set output path on the node parm (output_file kwarg doesn't
   252→            # work reliably for usdrender/karma ROPs)
   253→            for parm_name in ("outputimage", "picture"):
   254→                p = node.parm(parm_name)
   255→                if p:

   257→                    break
   258→
   259→            node.render(
   260→                frame_range=(cur, cur),
   261→                verbose=False,
   262→            )

   264→            # Karma XPU has a delayed file flush -- poll up to ~15s
   265→            for _ in range(60):

   272→                    "check if the output directory is writable and the renderer didn't error"
   273→                )
   274→            return out_path, node.path(), node_type, engine

   276→        import hdefereval

   290→    def _handle_set_keyframe(self, payload: Dict) -> Dict:
   291→        """Set a keyframe on a node parameter at a specific frame."""
   292→        if not HOU_AVAILABLE:
   293→            raise RuntimeError(_HOUDINI_UNAVAILABLE)
   294→        node_path = resolve_param(payload, "node")
   295→        parm_name = resolve_param(payload, "parm")

   315→            key.setValue(float(value))

   323→        return {

   331→        """Read and optionally modify render settings on a ROP or Karma node."""
   332→        if not HOU_AVAILABLE:

   343→        settings = {}
   344→        # Read current render settings
   345→        for parm in node.parms():
   346→            try:
   347→                # hou.Parm.eval() reads parameter value -- not Python eval()
   348→                val = parm.eval()  # noqa: S307
   349→                if isinstance(val, (int, float, str)):
   350→                    settings[parm.name()] = val
   351→            except Exception:
   352→                pass
   353→
   354→        # Apply overrides if provided
   355→        overrides = resolve_param_with_default(payload, "settings", {})
   356→        if isinstance(overrides, dict):
   357→            for k, v in sorted(overrides.items()):
   358→                p = node.parm(k)

   363→        return {"node": node_path, "settings": settings}
   364→
   365→    def _handle_wedge(self, payload: Dict) -> Dict:
   366→        """Run a TOPs/PDG wedge to explore parameter variations."""
   367→        if not HOU_AVAILABLE:
   368→            raise RuntimeError(_HOUDINI_UNAVAILABLE)

   370→        import hdefereval
   371→
   372→        top_path = resolve_param(payload, "node")  # TOP network or wedge node

   374→        values = resolve_param(payload, "values", required=False)

   419→    def _handle_tops_get_work_items(self, payload: Dict) -> Dict:
   420→        """Get work items from a TOP node with optional state filtering.
   421→
   422→        Returns work item details including id, index, name, state, cook time,
   423→        and optionally attributes. Useful for inspecting what a TOP node produced.
   424→        """
   425→        if not HOU_AVAILABLE:
   426→            raise RuntimeError(_HOUDINI_UNAVAILABLE)
   427→
   428→        import hdefereval
   429→
   430→        node_path = resolve_param(payload, "node")
   431→        state_filter = resolve_param_with_default(payload, "state_filter", "all")
   432→        include_attrs = resolve_param_with_default(payload, "include_attributes", True)
   433→        limit = resolve_param_with_default(payload, "limit", 100)
   434→
   435→        def _run():
   436→            node = hou.node(node_path)
   437→            if node is None:
   438→                raise ValueError(
   439→                    f"Couldn't find a node at {node_path} -- "
   440→                    "double-check the path exists"
   441→                )
   442→
   443→            pdg_node = node.getPDGNode()
   444→            if pdg_node is None:
   445→                raise ValueError(
   446→                    f"The node at {node_path} isn't a TOP node or hasn't been "
   447→                    "set up for PDG yet -- make sure it's inside a TOP network"
   448→                )
   449→
   450→            # Map state names to pdg.workItemState values
   451→            import pdg as _pdg
   452→            state_map = {
   453→                "cooked": _pdg.workItemState.CookedSuccess,
   454→                "failed": _pdg.workItemState.CookedFail,
   455→                "cooking": _pdg.workItemState.Cooking,
   456→                "scheduled": _pdg.workItemState.Scheduled,
   457→                "uncooked": _pdg.workItemState.Uncooked,
   458→                "cancelled": _pdg.workItemState.CookedCancel,
   459→            }
   460→
   461→            all_items = pdg_node.workItems
   462→            items = []
   463→            for wi in all_items:
   464→                # Apply state filter
   465→                if state_filter != "all":
   466→                    expected_state = state_map.get(state_filter.lower())
   467→                    if expected_state is not None and wi.state != expected_state:
   468→                        continue
   469→
   470→                item = {
   471→                    "id": wi.id,
   472→                    "index": wi.index,
   473→                    "name": wi.name,
   474→                    "state": wi.state.name if hasattr(wi.state, 'name') else str(wi.state),
   475→                    "cook_time": round_float(getattr(wi, 'cookTime', 0.0)),
   476→                }
   477→
   478→                if include_attrs:
   479→                    attrs = {}
   480→                    try:
   481→                        for attr in wi.attribs:
   482→                            try:
   483→                                attrs[attr.name] = attr.values()
   484→                            except Exception:
   485→                                attrs[attr.name] = str(attr)
   486→                    except Exception:
   487→                        pass
   488→                    item["attributes"] = attrs
   489→
   490→                items.append(item)
   491→                if len(items) >= int(limit):
   492→                    break
   493→
   494→            return {
   495→                "node": node_path,
   496→                "total_items": len(all_items),
   497→                "returned": len(items),
   498→                "filter": state_filter,
   499→                "items": items,
   500→            }
   501→
   502→        return hdefereval.executeInMainThreadWithResult(_run)

   533→

   535→            nodes = []

   544→
   545→                # Get work item counts by state if PDG node exists

   578→    def _handle_tops_get_cook_stats(self, payload: Dict) -> Dict:
   579→        """Get cook statistics for a TOP node or network.
   580→
   581→        For a single TOP node: work item counts by state and total cook time.
   582→        For a TOP network: aggregate stats across all child nodes.
   583→        """
   584→        if not HOU_AVAILABLE:
   585→            raise RuntimeError(_HOUDINI_UNAVAILABLE)
   586→
   587→        import hdefereval
   588→
   589→        node_path = resolve_param(payload, "node")
   590→
   591→        def _run():
   592→            node = hou.node(node_path)
   593→            if node is None:
   594→                raise ValueError(
   595→                    f"Couldn't find a node at {node_path} -- "
   596→                    "double-check the path exists"
   597→                )
   598→
   599→            cat = node.type().category().name()
   600→
   601→            def _node_stats(n):
   602→                """Get stats for a single TOP node."""
   603→                pdg_node = n.getPDGNode()
   604→                if pdg_node is None:
   605→                    return {"name": n.name(), "path": n.path(), "by_state": {}, "total_items": 0, "cook_time": 0.0}
   606→                by_state = {}
   607→                cook_times = []
   608→                for wi in pdg_node.workItems:
   609→                    state_name = wi.state.name if hasattr(wi.state, 'name') else str(wi.state)
   610→                    by_state[state_name] = by_state.get(state_name, 0) + 1
   611→                    cook_times.append(getattr(wi, 'cookTime', 0.0))
   612→                return {
   613→                    "name": n.name(),
   614→                    "path": n.path(),
   615→                    "by_state": dict(sorted(by_state.items())),
   616→                    "total_items": sum(by_state.values()),
   617→                    "cook_time": kahan_sum(cook_times),
   618→                }
   619→
   620→            if cat == "TopNet":
   621→                # Aggregate over children
   622→                node_stats = []
   623→                agg_by_state = {}
   624→                cook_times = []
   625→                total_items = 0
   626→                for child in node.children():
   627→                    s = _node_stats(child)
   628→                    node_stats.append(s)
   629→                    cook_times.append(s["cook_time"])
   630→                    total_items += s["total_items"]
   631→                    for state, count in sorted(s["by_state"].items()):
   632→                        agg_by_state[state] = agg_by_state.get(state, 0) + count
   633→                return {
   634→                    "node": node_path,
   635→                    "is_network": True,
   636→                    "total_items": total_items,
   637→                    "by_state": dict(sorted(agg_by_state.items())),
   638→                    "total_cook_time": kahan_sum(cook_times),
   639→                    "nodes": node_stats,
   640→                }
   641→            else:
   642→                s = _node_stats(node)
   643→                return {
   644→                    "node": node_path,
   645→                    "is_network": False,
   646→                    "total_items": s["total_items"],
   647→                    "by_state": s["by_state"],  # already sorted by _node_stats
   648→                    "total_cook_time": s["cook_time"],
   649→                    "nodes": [s],
   650→                }
   651→
   652→        return hdefereval.executeInMainThreadWithResult(_run)

   917→    def _handle_tops_setup_wedge(self, payload: Dict) -> Dict:
   918→        """Set up a Wedge TOP node for parameter variation exploration.
   919→
   920→        Creates a wedge node inside a TOP network and configures its
   921→        attributes (multiparm) for systematic parameter sweeps.
   922→        """
   923→        if not HOU_AVAILABLE:
   924→            raise RuntimeError(_HOUDINI_UNAVAILABLE)

   928→        topnet_path = resolve_param(payload, "topnet_path")
   929→        wedge_name = resolve_param_with_default(payload, "wedge_name", "wedge1")
   930→        attributes = resolve_param(payload, "attributes")
   931→
   932→        if not isinstance(attributes, list) or len(attributes) == 0:
   933→            raise ValueError(
   934→                "The 'attributes' parameter should be a list of attribute definitions "
   935→                "(each with name, type, start, end, steps)"
   936→            )
   937→
   938→        def _run():
   939→            node = hou.node(topnet_path)
   940→            if node is None:
   941→                raise ValueError(
   942→                    f"Couldn't find a node at {topnet_path} -- "
   943→                    "double-check the path exists"
   944→                )
   945→
   946→            cat = node.type().category().name()
   947→            if cat not in ("TopNet",):
   948→                raise ValueError(
   949→                    f"The node at {topnet_path} is a {cat} node, not a TOP network -- "
   950→                    "point to a topnet node (e.g. '/obj/topnet1')"
   951→                )
   952→
   953→            wedge_node = node.createNode("wedge", wedge_name)
   954→            wedge_node.moveToGoodPosition()
   955→
   956→            # Configure wedge attributes via multiparm
   957→            sorted_attrs = sorted(attributes, key=lambda a: a.get("name", ""))
   958→            num_attrs = len(sorted_attrs)
   959→            multiparm = wedge_node.parm("wedgeattributes")
   960→            if multiparm:
   961→                multiparm.set(num_attrs)
   962→
   963→            total_variations = 1
   964→            attr_results = []
   965→            for i, attr in enumerate(sorted_attrs):
   966→                idx = i + 1  # 1-indexed multiparm
   967→                attr_name = attr.get("name", f"attr_{i}")
   968→                attr_type = attr.get("type", "float")
   969→                start = attr.get("start", 0)
   970→                end = attr.get("end", 1)
   971→                steps = attr.get("steps", 5)
   972→
   973→                # Set wedge attribute parameters
   974→                name_parm = wedge_node.parm(f"name{idx}")
   975→                if name_parm:
   976→                    name_parm.set(attr_name)
   977→
   978→                type_parm = wedge_node.parm(f"type{idx}")
   979→                if type_parm:
   980→                    type_map = {"float": 0, "int": 1, "string": 2}
   981→                    type_parm.set(type_map.get(attr_type, 0))
   982→
   983→                start_parm = wedge_node.parm(f"range{idx}x")
   984→                if start_parm:
   985→                    start_parm.set(float(start))
   986→
   987→                end_parm = wedge_node.parm(f"range{idx}y")
   988→                if end_parm:
   989→                    end_parm.set(float(end))
   990→
   991→                steps_parm = wedge_node.parm(f"steps{idx}")
   992→                if steps_parm:
   993→                    steps_parm.set(int(steps))
   994→
   995→                total_variations *= int(steps)
   996→                attr_results.append({

  1015→
  1016→        Cooks each node in order and collects per-node results including
  1017→        status, work item counts, and cook times. Uses kahan_sum for
  1018→        stable total cook time aggregation (He2025).

  1021→            raise RuntimeError(_HOUDINI_UNAVAILABLE)

  1030→            raise ValueError(
  1031→                "The 'node_paths' parameter should be a list of TOP node paths"
  1032→            )

  1034→        def _run():
  1035→            results = []
  1036→            cook_times = []
  1037→            by_state = {}
  1038→            errors = []
  1039→
  1040→            for node_path in node_paths:
  1041→                node = hou.node(node_path)
  1042→                if node is None:
  1043→                    err = f"Couldn't find a node at {node_path}"
  1044→                    if stop_on_error:
  1045→                        raise ValueError(err)
  1046→                    results.append({
  1047→                        "node": node_path,
  1048→                        "status": "error",
  1049→                        "error": err,
  1050→                        "cook_time": 0.0,
  1051→                    })
  1052→                    errors.append(node_path)
  1053→                    continue
  1054→
  1055→                pdg_node = node.getPDGNode()
  1056→                if pdg_node is None:
  1057→                    err = f"The node at {node_path} isn't a TOP node"
  1058→                    if stop_on_error:
  1059→                        raise ValueError(err)
  1060→                    results.append({
  1061→                        "node": node_path,
  1062→                        "status": "error",
  1063→                        "error": err,
  1064→                        "cook_time": 0.0,
  1065→                    })
  1066→                    errors.append(node_path)
  1067→                    continue
  1068→
  1069→                t0 = time.monotonic()
  1070→                try:
  1071→                    node.cook(block=bool(blocking))
  1072→                    elapsed = time.monotonic() - t0
  1073→                    item_count = len(pdg_node.workItems)
  1074→
  1075→                    # Collect per-node state counts
  1076→                    node_states = {}
  1077→                    for wi in pdg_node.workItems:
  1078→                        sname = wi.state.name if hasattr(wi.state, 'name') else str(wi.state)
  1079→                        node_states[sname] = node_states.get(sname, 0) + 1
  1080→
  1081→                    for sname, count in sorted(node_states.items()):
  1082→                        by_state[sname] = by_state.get(sname, 0) + count
  1083→
  1084→                    results.append({
  1085→                        "node": node_path,
  1086→                        "status": "cooked" if blocking else "cooking",
  1087→                        "work_items": item_count,
  1088→                        "cook_time": round_float(elapsed),
  1089→                    })
  1090→                    cook_times.append(elapsed)
  1091→                except Exception as e:
  1092→                    elapsed = time.monotonic() - t0
  1093→                    err = str(e)
  1094→                    if stop_on_error:
  1095→                        raise
  1096→                    results.append({
  1097→                        "node": node_path,
  1098→                        "status": "error",
  1099→                        "error": err,
  1100→                        "cook_time": round_float(elapsed),
  1101→                    })
  1102→                    cook_times.append(elapsed)
  1103→                    errors.append(node_path)
  1104→
  1105→            total = kahan_sum(cook_times)
  1106→            cooked = sum(1 for r in results if r["status"] in ("cooked", "cooking"))
  1107→            summary = f"Cooked {cooked}/{len(node_paths)} nodes"
  1108→            if errors:
  1109→                summary += f", {len(errors)} error(s)"
  1110→
  1111→            return {
  1112→                "nodes": results,
  1113→                "total_cook_time": round_float(total),
  1114→                "by_state": dict(sorted(by_state.items())),
  1115→                "summary": summary,
  1116→            }

  1380→    def _handle_validate_frame(self, payload: Dict) -> Dict:

  1384→        and firefly (saturation) artifacts. Uses OpenImageIO for fast C++-level

  1390→        threshold_overrides = resolve_param_with_default(payload, "thresholds", None) or {}

  1397→            if invalid:
  1398→                raise ValueError(
  1399→                    f"Unknown check(s): {', '.join(invalid)}. "
  1400→                    f"Available checks: {', '.join(_VALIDATE_CHECKS)}"
  1401→                )
  1402→            check_set = set(requested_checks)
  1403→        else:
  1404→            check_set = set(_VALIDATE_CHECKS)
  1405→
  1406→        # Merge thresholds
  1407→        thresholds = dict(_VALIDATE_DEFAULTS)
  1408→        for k, v in sorted(threshold_overrides.items()):
  1409→            if k in thresholds:

  1423→                    "valid": False,
  1424→                    "image_path": image_path,
  1425→                    "resolution": None,
  1426→                    "channels": None,
  1427→                    "format": None,
  1428→                    "checks": dict(sorted(checks_result.items())),
  1429→                    "summary": f"Frame has 1 issue(s): file_integrity",
  1430→                    "oiio_available": False,

  1433→        # --- Try to load OIIO ---

  1435→        try:
  1436→            import OpenImageIO as oiio
  1437→        except ImportError:
  1438→            try:
  1439→                import oiio as oiio
  1440→            except ImportError:
  1441→                pass

  1446→                "valid": len(issues) == 0,
  1447→                "image_path": image_path,
  1448→                "resolution": None,
  1449→                "channels": None,
  1450→                "format": None,
  1451→                "checks": dict(sorted(checks_result.items())),
  1452→                "summary": "OIIO unavailable -- only file integrity checked",
  1453→                "oiio_available": False,

  1478→        fmt_str = str(spec.format)

  1481→        # --- Compute pixel stats via ImageBuf ---

  1483→        stats = oiio.ImageBufAlgo.computePixelStats(buf)
  1484→

  1487→        pixels = None

  1490→        if need_pixels:

  1495→            if total_pixels > 8_000_000:

  1498→            else:

  1507→        if "black_frame" in check_set:

  1512→                "value": round(mean_lum, 6),

  1523→            passed = total_bad == 0

  1525→                "passed": passed,
  1526→                "value": int(total_bad),
  1527→                "threshold": 0,
  1528→                "detail": "No NaN/Inf pixels" if passed else f"Found {int(nan_count)} NaN and {int(inf_count)} Inf values",

  1530→            if not passed:
  1531→                issues.append("nan_check")
  1532→
  1533→        if "clipping" in check_set and pixels is not None:
  1534→            import numpy as np
  1535→            thresh_pct = thresholds["clipping_pct"]
  1536→            rgb = pixels[:, :, :rgb_channels]
  1537→            clipped = int(np.sum(rgb >= 1.0))

1→"""
     2→Synapse Recipe Registry
     3→
     4→Pre-built, pre-approved multi-step operation templates.
     5→Recipes execute at Tier 0 speed by expanding triggers into
     6→sequences of SynapseCommands without any LLM involvement.
     7→
     8→Artists can register custom recipes via registry.register().
     9→"""
    10→
    11→import json
    12→import re
    13→from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    14→from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple, Any
    15→
    16→from ..core.protocol import SynapseCommand
    17→from ..core.gates import GateLevel
    18→from ..core.determinism import deterministic_uuid
    19→
    20→
    21→@dataclass
    22→class RecipeStep:
    23→    """A single step in a recipe template."""
    24→    action: str                        # CommandType value
    25→    payload_template: Dict[str, Any]   # Values may contain {placeholders}
    26→    gate_level: GateLevel = GateLevel.REVIEW
    27→    output_var: str = ""               # If set, response data stored as ${var}.{field}
    28→
    29→    def instantiate(self, params: Dict[str, str]) -> SynapseCommand:
    30→        """Fill placeholders and return a SynapseCommand."""
    31→        payload = {}
    32→        for key, value in sorted(self.payload_template.items()):
    33→            if isinstance(value, str) and "{" in value:
    34→                payload[key] = value.format(**params)
    35→            else:
    36→                payload[key] = value
    37→
    38→        return SynapseCommand(
    39→            type=self.action,
    40→            id=deterministic_uuid(
    41→                f"recipe:{self.action}:{json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, default=str)}", "cmd"
    42→            ),
    43→            payload=payload,
    44→        )
    45→
    46→    def instantiate_with_vars(self, variables: Dict[str, str]) -> SynapseCommand:
    47→        """Fill placeholders using accumulated variables (supports $var.field syntax)."""
    48→        payload = {}
    49→        for key, value in sorted(self.payload_template.items()):
    50→            if isinstance(value, str):
    51→                # Replace $var.field references first
    52→                resolved = value
    53→                for var_key in sorted(variables.keys(), key=len, reverse=True):
    54→                    resolved = resolved.replace(var_key, str(variables[var_key]))
    55→                # Then standard {param} placeholders
    56→                if "{" in resolved:
    57→                    resolved = resolved.format(**{
    58→                        k: v for k, v in sorted(variables.items())
    59→                        if not k.startswith("$")
    60→                    })
    61→                payload[key] = resolved
    62→            else:
    63→                payload[key] = value
    64→
    65→        return SynapseCommand(
    66→            type=self.action,
    67→            id=deterministic_uuid(
    68→                f"recipe:{self.action}:{json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, default=str)}", "cmd"
    69→            ),
    70→            payload=payload,
    71→        )
    72→
    73→
    74→@dataclass
    75→class Recipe:
    76→    """A pre-built multi-step operation template."""
    77→    name: str
    78→    description: str
    79→    triggers: List[str]                # Regex patterns (case-insensitive)
    80→    parameters: List[str]              # Named capture groups expected
    81→    steps: List[RecipeStep]
    82→    gate_level: GateLevel = GateLevel.REVIEW
    83→    category: str = "general"
    84→
    85→    _compiled: List["re.Pattern[str]"] = field(default_factory=list, repr=False)
    86→
    87→    def __post_init__(self):
    88→        self._compiled = [
    89→            re.compile(t, re.IGNORECASE) for t in self.triggers
    90→        ]
    91→
    92→    def match(self, text: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, str]]:
    93→        """
    94→        Try to match text against trigger patterns.
    95→
    96→        Returns extracted parameters on match, None otherwise.
    97→        """
    98→        text = text.strip()
    99→        for pattern in self._compiled:
   100→            m = pattern.match(text)
   101→            if m:
   102→                params = m.groupdict()
   103→                # Fill defaults for missing optional params
   104→                for p in self.parameters:
   105→                    if p not in params or params[p] is None:
   106→                        params[p] = ""
   107→                return params
   108→        return None
   109→
   110→    def instantiate(self, params: Dict[str, str]) -> List[SynapseCommand]:
   111→        """Fill templates with extracted params, return command list."""
   112→        return [step.instantiate(params) for step in self.steps]
   113→
   114→    def execute(
   115→        self,
   116→        params: Dict[str, str],
   117→        command_fn,
   118→    ) -> List[Tuple[SynapseCommand, Any]]:
   119→        """Execute recipe with data flow between steps.
   120→
   121→        Each step can declare output_var. After execution, response data
   122→        fields become ${var}.{field} variables available to later steps.
   123→
   124→        Args:
   125→            params: Initial parameters from trigger match.
   126→            command_fn: Callable(SynapseCommand) -> SynapseResponse.
   127→
   128→        Returns:
   129→            List of (command, response) tuples.
   130→        """
   131→        variables: Dict[str, str] = dict(params)
   132→        results: List[Tuple[SynapseCommand, Any]] = []
   133→        for step in self.steps:
   134→            cmd = step.instantiate_with_vars(variables)
   135→            resp = command_fn(cmd)
   136→            results.append((cmd, resp))
   137→            if step.output_var and hasattr(resp, "data") and isinstance(resp.data, dict):
   138→                for k, v in sorted(resp.data.items()):  # sorted: He2025
   139→                    variables[f"${step.output_var}.{k}"] = str(v)

1→"""
     2→Synapse Workflow Planner
     3→
     4→Decomposes complex natural-language requests into multi-step
     5→operation plans. Sits between Recipe (exact match) and Tier 0 (regex)
     6→in the routing cascade.
     7→
     8→Unlike recipes (static templates), the planner:
     9→- Detects composite intents ("set up X with Y and Z")
    10→- Composes steps dynamically from a knowledge-driven operation graph
    11→- Supports optional/conditional steps based on detected modifiers
    12→- Returns a plan as a list of SynapseCommands
    13→
    14→The planner is entirely pattern-based (no LLM call). It recognizes
    15→workflow structures and fills them from a catalog of known operations.
    16→"""
    17→
    18→import re
    19→import logging
    20→from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    21→from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple, Any
    22→
    23→from ..core.protocol import SynapseCommand
    24→from ..core.determinism import deterministic_uuid
    25→
    26→logger = logging.getLogger("synapse.planner")
    27→
    28→
    29→# ------------------------------------------------------------------
    30→# Operation catalog — atomic operations the planner can compose
    31→# ------------------------------------------------------------------
    32→
    33→@dataclass
    34→class Operation:
    35→    """A single atomic operation the planner can insert into a plan."""
    36→    name: str
    37→    action: str                          # CommandType value
    38→    payload_template: Dict[str, Any]
    39→    description: str = ""
    40→    optional: bool = False
    41→
    42→
    43→@dataclass
    44→class WorkflowPlan:
    45→    """A composed multi-step plan ready for execution."""
    46→    name: str
    47→    description: str
    48→    steps: List[SynapseCommand]
    49→    metadata: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    50→
    51→
    52→# ------------------------------------------------------------------
    53→# Intent detection — recognizes composite workflow requests
    54→# ------------------------------------------------------------------
    55→
    56→# Workflow intent patterns: (regex, workflow_key, param_extractor_groups)
    57→_WORKFLOW_INTENTS: List[Tuple[re.Pattern, str, List[str]]] = [
    58→    # Cloth/Vellum simulation with modifiers
    59→    (re.compile(
    60→        r"(?:set up|setup|create|build)\s+(?:a\s+)?(?:complete\s+)?(?:vellum\s+)?"
    61→        r"cloth\s+(?:sim(?:ulation)?\s+)?"
    62→        r"(?:with\s+(?P<modifiers>.+))?",
    63→        re.IGNORECASE,
    64→    ), "cloth_pipeline", ["modifiers"]),
    65→
    66→    # RBD destruction with modifiers
    67→    (re.compile(
    68→        r"(?:set up|setup|create|build)\s+(?:a\s+)?(?:complete\s+)?(?:rbd\s+)?"
    69→        r"destruction\s+(?:pipeline|sequence|sim(?:ulation)?)?\s*"
    70→        r"(?:with\s+(?P<modifiers>.+))?",
    71→        re.IGNORECASE,
    72→    ), "destruction_pipeline", ["modifiers"]),
    73→
    74→    # Pyro with modifiers
    75→    (re.compile(
    76→        r"(?:set up|setup|create|build)\s+(?:a\s+)?(?:complete\s+)?(?:pyro\s+)?"
    77→        r"(?:fire|smoke|explosion)\s+(?:sim(?:ulation)?\s+)?"
    78→        r"(?:with\s+(?P<modifiers>.+))?",
    79→        re.IGNORECASE,
    80→    ), "pyro_pipeline", ["modifiers"]),
    81→
    82→    # Lighting rig with modifiers
    83→    (re.compile(
    84→        r"(?:"
    85→        r"(?:set up|setup|create|build)\s+(?:a\s+)?(?:complete\s+)?lighting\s+(?:rig|setup)"
    86→        r"|light\s+(?:the\s+)?scene"
    87→        r")\s*"
    88→        r"(?:for\s+(?P<mood>broadcast|dramatic|product|horror|overcast))?\s*"
    89→        r"(?:with\s+(?P<modifiers>.+))?",
    90→        re.IGNORECASE,
    91→    ), "lighting_pipeline", ["mood", "modifiers"]),
    92→
    93→    # Full render pipeline
    94→    (re.compile(
    95→        r"(?:set up|setup|create|build)\s+(?:a\s+)?(?:complete\s+)?(?:full\s+)?"
    96→        r"render\s+pipeline\s*"
    97→        r"(?:with\s+(?P<modifiers>.+))?",
    98→        re.IGNORECASE,
    99→    ), "render_pipeline", ["modifiers"]),
   100→
   101→    # Ocean with interaction
   102→    (re.compile(
   103→        r"(?:set up|setup|create|build)\s+(?:an?\s+)?(?:complete\s+)?ocean\s+"
   104→        r"(?:with\s+(?P<modifiers>.+))",
   105→        re.IGNORECASE,
   106→    ), "ocean_pipeline", ["modifiers"]),
   107→]
   108→
   109→# Modifier keywords that toggle optional steps
   110→_MODIFIER_KEYWORDS = {
   111→    # Cloth pipeline
   112→    "collision": "add_collision",
   113→    "collider": "add_collision",
   114→    "drape": "add_drape",

   116→    "cache": "add_cache",
   117→    "caching": "add_cache",
   118→    "pin": "add_pin",
   119→    "pinning": "add_pin",
   120→    "wind": "add_wind",
   121→    # Destruction pipeline
   122→    "debris": "add_debris",
